If you asked me, I would have told you—without hesitation—that my husband, Alpha Greg, loved me.
Until this morning.
“Run it again,” my eyes were watery “please,” I begged but the doctor only placed a hand on my shoulders.
“I’m sorry,” he said, I could catch the pity in his tone.
I refused to accept that.
“But one more ovarian stimulation could destroy your uterine lining, it’s best this way,” he said but I was shaking my head now.
How did he know why was best and what was not?
Did he understand what a barren Luna was worth in this pack?
I gritted my teeth, pain now visible around my eyes as I tried to sit up forcefully.
His hands curled around my shoulders again, pressing me down with an urgency I couldn’t believe.
“Your highness!” His tone incredulous
“B–But I want a child,” I pleaded “The fourth time could be my lucky charm. Please,” I begged but the doctors eyes had filled with so much empathy, my body was close to sobs.

“Or your last,” he slowly said “please, your highness,”  He cautioned and my body finally let me rest. Not out of will but out of exhaustion.

“You should rest for a few weeks. No intercourse,” he warned and that prompted me to sit up slowly.

“No sex?!” I questioned, already biting my lips in a panic. If there was anything Greg and I still had, it was our zeal for intimacy.

To go without it felt like losing the last place we still met as equals. The doctor gave me a look of concern and my shoulders sagged in response.

How was I going to tell Greg?

I slid off of the hospital bed and arranged my clothing. Greg was supposed to follow me to the hospital today but after my second ovarian stimulation had failed, I could understand why he suddenly went deep into work.

Greg was the head of the southern Ironclaw pack and he had already crossed lines by coming with me twice.

Which was why this news was almost scary to tell. Despite Greg telling me not to worry about having kids, that the right time would come from the moon goddess I couldn’t help myself.

I was already ona
thin ice, marrying a high ranking alpha knowing what I was — a human — and now I was not even close to conceiving an heir.

I wiped the tears that fell freely from my face. I wished Greg was here anyway. He would know the right thing to say to cheer me up. I walked out of the room and the doctor met me upfront, his hands holding a delicate substance wrapped up nicely.

My brows furrowed almost immediately as he handed it to me.
“Hand this to a seer and perhaps the moon goddess can help,” he said and I hesitated for a bit.

“What is it?” I asked.

“A prescription. A way to manage your…” he trailed and my eyes looked up at him. A subtle hint of anger coursing through my veins.

“Medically, your highness and I say this with utmost respect. There is nothing we can do,” he said and my chest constructed painfully.

I didn’t know when I took the delicate wrapping.  My hands shook for a bit and a coldness seeped through my clothing the moment he left.

Was this what my life had come to? From doctors to seers?

My eyes watered, my strength failing as I tried to gather myself. I couldn’t be a clobbering mess before Greg. I didn’t want him knowing how crushed I was even as he managed to exact a perfect show of self control and calm.

I missed him. His voice, his arms the way they wrapped around me and let heat spread through out my body.

I could almost feel him, closing my eyes and letting the memory come into existence when a voice came through. My eyes snapped open in disbelief.

“Where are you?” a voice murmured.

I turned and froze.

Greg stood at the entrance of the obstetrics ward, not searching, not panicked. Waiting.

As if he had known I would be here.

Without thinking, I rushed forward.

How did he know that I needed him?

The questions were piling, my eyes taking note that there were no guards with him. My brain finding that detail a bit odd but overruling it with joy.

I was so close to him when he turned, his hands outstretched. My body seemed to go slow, confused. Why was his hands stretching towards the wrong direction.

Didn’t he see me?

My mouth opened to cry out his name but my throat suddenly closed in a strangled gasp as a figure emerged from a room not far from the entrance where Greg stood.

She stepped into view, round-bellied, glowing and unmistakably pregnant.

Greg’s hands closed around her waist.

“What did the doctors say?” he asked quietly. His hand rested at her back not possessive, not loving, but practiced.

The kind of touch that came from habit, not affection.He helped her sit delicately, before taking a seat of his own.

I leaned forward without thinking , evesdropping but her next words broke everything I had.

“The doctors said the twins were doing well and were due any time now,” she said, looking up at Greg while my eyes had grown blurry.

He smiled sheepishly and rubbed her tummy.
At first, I tasted bile and then the nausea tore me apart.

The heartbreak and betrayal mixed violently in my heart, every breath I took was a war front between confronting what I had seen and claiming insanity.

I had tried my best,  accepting extreme treatments. Talked down by Greg’s mother, called a gold digger despite everyone knowing how Greg and I met.

I had saved his life once. I wondered now if that was my mistake.

“I heard her highness came around today,” a voice suddenly said from behind me. My eyes moved stealthily towards the voice.

The nurse was turned away, well hidden but her voice was loud.

“Some women just aren’t meant to be Lunas,” one murmured.

“Especially not humans,” another replied quietly. I gasped in shock.

The women heard me and turned towards me, their gaze sharp. My skin crawled and my palms turned to fists.

I made a move, unsure what my next step was going to be when their eyes suddenly turned hollow. They shrunk in size and it wasn’t until they began to stammer as their gaze moved past me that I realized who they were afraid of.

A figure moved silently towards them, his stride filled with power and anger.

“Leave,” he said coldly.

No raised voice. No fury. Just authority.

My mouth was agape with nothing coming out of it. The girls were scrambling in fear as he turned around. When his eyes met mine, I could see the instant regret in them.

I couldn’t stay any longer. I had confirmed what I now knew. Greg, the love of my life was nothing but a liar.

Hands grabbed my wrist and spun me around. I collided into his chest but my eyes were watery.

“Come with me,” he whispered and held me close to him. Walking with him till we were no longer in the discomfort of the hospital.

We were seated in the confines of our carriage when I snatched my arm from his grip and faced the window. I would sooner have an accident and die than listen to what he thought he had to say.

“Layla?” He called gently. Using the same fake concern that he’s been using all these years.

I was already crying silently. I had left everything I knew for him and this was how he betrayed me?

His hands molded into mine and slowly, hands wrapped around my waist and drew me into him.

“I know,” he whispered as my body shook with sobs. My body, exhausted from the pain and heartbreak was no match for him as he carefully held my chin and made my body respond to him.

“I can explain,” he said gently, his own eyes now bloodshot. He almost looked like he was suffering.

“This isn’t what you think,” he said hoarsely.

I laughed, a broken sound. My throat was dry and my soul was withering with heartbreak.

“Then tell me what it is.” I demanded, my voice steady despite my heart racing.

He looked away. Regret in his eyes.

“I can’t.” He said. The silence was worse than any confession.

“I did what was required of me,” he said finally.
“And I will handle the consequences.”

I wanted to rip out my own hair. Consequences? Really?

“Including me?” I asked carefully.

His jaw tightened but he didn’t answer. “I never meant to hurt your feelings,” he finished and my body went numb. His lack of a good reason made it so much worse.

I had endured everything to keep him and all this time, he had endured me for his throne.

His hands moved to touch my cheek and I flinched. He didn’t notice.

He tried to wrap his hands around me. Our signature move that almost always led to intimacy.

Disgust tore me apart as my hands acted out of will, pushing him away from me.

The world went quiet for a minute as all these while I have never looked Greg in the eyes.

At that moment, I understood something clearly.
Love that must lie is not love. It was control.

My eyes locked in with his as I decided my fate.
“No, husband. Let’s get a divorce,”

Chapter 2
LAYLA

Slowly, Greg’s hands crept around my wrist. At first it almost seemed as though he wanted to massage my pulse point but it turned stiff.

A tight smile creased his face as he chuckled softly.
“Don’t make silly jokes, Layla,” he said but I didn’t join him to smile.

I snatched my hands from his grip, his eyes widened in surprise.
“And who said I was joking?” I questioned with a sharp tilt of my head to show defiance.

For a moment, he didn’t speak. His eyes held surprise and questions. The nerve.

I straightened my back, eyes not leaving his and said “spouses should be honest with each other”

He scoffed then. His display of annoyance vivid while my throat tightened in response as my hands wringed around each other. The stabbing feeling of his betrayal still in my heart.

“There were other options,” I said. “You chose silence instead.”

My eyes were blurry and sight became painful but I forced my gaze on him. Still in disbelief that he could do something like this but Greg just stared at me, his eyes emotionless but angry at the same time.

“You could have told me. I could have considered it,” I said but he scoffed.

“You were not ready to listen,” he snorted and anger exploded in my chest.

“Did you tell me?” I questioned in irritation. All of it. The pain. The humiliation. For nothing.

“You let everyone treat me like I was uninhabitable.”I spat.

Greg gave a tired sigh “If it matters,” he said, tired, “there’s no relationship. She’s only a surrogate.” I let out a forceful scoff.

“A surrogate?” I questioned. Did he know the meaning of surrogacy or was I just gullible?

His silence hit me where it hurt the most and I let out a broken laugh.

I must be really stupid if he thought, telling me that crap would make me forgive him.

“And since when did werewolf start performing IVF?” I questioned and his jaw tightened. His gaze moved from my face.

“No! Since when did strange women carry a baby without the mother’s help?” I questioned angrily.

“Answer me” I demanded but Greg’s face was turned away completely. Something in my chest had tightened. The car had gone quiet, save for my angry breathing and his quiet one.

The air was tense as my mind spun so many questions until it landed on one that caused my throat to tighten.

“Did you sleep with her?” I asked calmly. I didn’t need to see his facial reaction to recognize the thread of guilt.

My head slumped in sorrow. I’ve been a fool.
Without thinking, I opened the door and walked out.

“Layla, come back. We can talk about this,” he called after me but I had nothing more to say. It was obvious, this marriage had been over long ago. I was just now being informed.

I don’t know how I got back to the palace but the instant I got back to our chambers, I moved on instinct, pulling my things into a box like my body had decided before my mind caught up.

My eyes hurt, exhaustion ravaged my body but my legs and hands kept going. I wouldn’t spend another minute in a place where I was publicly praised but privately mocked and unwanted.

I had placed a bunch of clothes inside a box when my phone buzzed loudly. I ignored it and kept going, determined to be back to the human world before nightfall.

The buzzing of my phone was incessant. I attempted to grab it but stopped myself, determined more than ever to finish my task but I I gave an angry sigh and snatched my phone, missing a call by mere seconds.

Accidentally, I opened his messages and my eyes read through them in increased annoyance and irritation.

Greg:
I know you’re confused. I know you feel wronged. But please believe me, I love you. I only love you.
Another message came through before I could breathe.
From the elders.
A warning disguised as concern.
They reminded me that allowing a human to be Luna had already been an exception. That I should not make trouble. That I should not hold the Alpha back any further.
I stared at the screen.
I was the only one in the pack with a phone. The only one who couldn’t mindlink. The only one who had to read betrayal instead of feeling it soften through shared thoughts.
I tossed the phone onto the bed.
The suitcase lay open at my feet. Every item inside it carried him. Gifts he’d chosen, clothes he liked me in, a life arranged around his presence. My vision blurred before I could stop it.
I sat on the edge of the bed and finally broke.
Tears came hard and fast, stealing my breath. I pressed my hand to my mouth, trying to stay quiet, but the sound escaped anyway. I felt so small, ruined and nothing like a Luna.
He loved me. I knew that. There were too many memories that proved it. The nights he stayed awake when I couldn’t sleep, the way he shielded me in public, the gentleness he never showed anyone else.
I believed in that love.
But how was I supposed to accept that my husband had been with another woman?
Had I really held him back?
Was this simply the price of being human?
I shook my head, the tears still streaming down. My heart was pounding heavily. Hands placed against my sternum to try to calm my breathing but a dull discomfort twisted low in my stomach.
I frowned, pressing my palm there absentmindedly. My appetite had been strange for days. Everything felt off. I’d blamed it on stress… on werewolf food… on anything that didn’t require me to think too deeply.
The sensation passed, leaving unease behind when a knock sounded at the door.
“Layla?”
I looked up, eyes burning.
My best friend, Portia,  stood there, worry written plainly across her face.
“Are you okay?”
I didn’t answer. I didn’t know how.

Chapter 3
LAYLA POV

I sat on the edge of the bed, staring at the half-packed suitcase, when a frantic knock pulled me from my daze. Before I could respond, the door burst open and there stood Mina, her chest heaving like she'd run the entire way from the pack hospital.

"Tell me it's not true," she gasped, rushing to sit beside me, grabbing my hands. "Tell me those rumors are just pack gossip."

I couldn't speak. The moment I looked at her face with genuine concern etched in every line, the tears I'd been holding back finally spilled over. Bestfriend  pulled me into a hug, and I broke down against her shoulder, telling her everything between sobs.

When I finally pulled back, wiping my face with trembling hands, the words tumbled out before I could stop them. "Bestfriend, what if they're right? What if I really am holding him back?"

Her eyes widened. "Don't you dare say that."

"But think about it," I pressed, my voice cracking. "I'm human in a world of werewolves. I can't mindlink, I can't shift, I can't even give him the child everyone expects. What use am I to him? To this pack?”

Bestfriend  grabbed my shoulders firmly, forcing me to meet her gaze. "Stop it. Just stop. You listen to me, alright? You were not always like this. Before you came here, before him, you were something. Remember? You told me so. Don't bring yourself down because of what these people think.”

I was better.

I was the one many people looked up to, j was someone, I had a good job that paid me so well, I led teams, ran campaigns, made decisions that actually mattered, my opinions mattered, and I loved it.

The challenge, the pressure, the satisfaction of pulling off something difficult, the satisfaction of meeting expectations. I was better, until I met him. He was so sincere, so passionate. Promised me the world, promised to love me forever. He was different, unlike anyone I've ever seen, and I believed him, I believed his promises, quit my job without a second thought, left everything behind, and followed him here.

He was my home, and wherever he went, I was there with him.

"You're going to be fine, I promise," Bestfriend  said. "If he's anything like you hoped, I know everything’s going to be fine."

"Maybe." I pulled my hands away, wrapping my arms around myself. "But now look at me. I don't work, I don't contribute, I don't do anything except wait for him to come home. I gave up everything that made me... me. And for what? Am I that much of a burden?”

“Maybe everything would change if I go back? I'd be better again, I would find my purpose, maybe then, then he'll see me for me again, the human he fell in love with.”

Bestfriend  turned to her sharply. “That…that'll be a good idea, I think. At least you won't spend all day thinking about all this. It's affecting your health.”

Could I really? After all these years?

What would he think of me then? Changed? Will that remind him of our past?

I reached for the TV remote, desperate for distraction when Bestfriend 's hand shot out, grabbing my wrist.

"Don't," she tightened her grip on my arm. “The last thing you need right now is staring at the screen.”

I stared at her, then at the screen. "Bestfriend , my eyes are fine, I don't need you to worry about them."

"I know. But just—maybe read a book instead, or—"

“A book won't take my mind off what's bothering me, Bestfriend . I know you're worried but I'll be fine with this.”I pulled free and turned on the television, switching through the channels until one caught my attention.

The werewolf news channel filled the screen with confusing texts all over it. For a moment I was confused. The announcement emblazoned across the bottom, going back and forth.

SOUTHERN PACK ALPHA TO WELCOME PURE-BLOOD HEIR.

Wha—what?

I stood up slowly, taking in the unending sight. On screen, reporters swarmed the streets of our pack territory, microphones thrust at passing werewolves. A burly man with thick stubble grinned at the camera as though he was a celebrity. "About damn time, if you ask me. That human Luna's been barren for years. Nice to see the Alpha finally doing what's right for the pack."

“My grandmother always said humans and werewolves shouldn't mix. Look at the proof—can't even produce a single pup. This new woman got proper bloodlines. That's the kind of Luna we need."

“Did you see her?” another wolf chimed in, young and eager. "Hailey, I mean. Gorgeous shape, strong presence. Everyone knows she's had her eye on the Alpha forever. Wouldn't surprise me if this arrangement turns into something more permanent. Would be better for everyone.”

The reporter smiled knowingly. "Many pack members seem to share that hope. And the pure-blood heir from noble lineage will certainly strengthen the pack's future."

Wha—

What?

I stumbled back, sitting back down. The remote slipped from my fingers, clattering to the floor and Bestfriend  quickly grabbed it, switched off the TV, and knelt before me.

“I'm sorry," she whispered. "You shouldn't have to see that.”

“They talk about me like I'm nothing.”

Was that how they saw me?

A useless being by their alpha's side?

“Like I'm a parasite, clinging to him, dragging him down. Years. I've been here for years, and that's all I am to them?”

Bestfriend 's eyes glistened. "You're not—"

"I am to them, Bestfriend . Isn't that obvious." I turned to her sharply. “What was I expecting? You can't expect two beings together, Bestfriend , I don't think it's ever happened.”

I'd promised to break off things if he ever cheated on me.

And I hoped. I hoped he remembered that, I hoped he realized how deeply he's hurt me.
Or was he really doing all this because I was holding him back? Was he forced to choose a surrogate? He had promised me he felt nothing for her and only saw her as a surrogate.

But I hoped dearly, he meant it.

"Have you…Have you thought about divorce?” Bestfriend  massaged my shoulders.

Divorce?

Walking away from years of marriage, of love, of promises?

Have I considered leaving the man I considered my life? A part of me?

Of all the time we spent together, the promises he made to me? Can I ever leave that? Will I be able to? Can I bear the pain?

I took a deep shaky breath and stood up slowly. "I need to see him first.”

I need to look him in the eyes and ask him directly. I need to know where I stood? If he still remembers me or if I'm latching on to a broken thread.

Bestfriend  nodded slowly, helping me. “Come on, I'll drive you. My brother dropped me off, his car's still outside."

We got into the car and made our way to the office. Passing by Werewolves lined along the streets, some gathered around portable screens showing the news, others simply celebrated openly.

"Finally, an heir worth having!"

"Did you see Hailey's announcement? Stunning, absolutely stunning. That's Luna material."

When we reached the pack's office building, a towering structure of stone and glass, Bestfriend  touched my shoulder stopping me. “I can come up with you if you want.”

“No.”I shook my head. I had to do this alone.

Being called a human like it's a disease is enough, I couldn't make them think same of Bestfriend  or that I can't face my fears without people to support me. "I'll be fine."

She hesitated, but nodded anyway . "I'll wait right here. Take all the time you need."

I walked through the massive doors, approaching the reception desk. The beta on duty looked up, startled.

"State your business," He began, then recognition flickered across his face. "Oh…”

“I’m here to see him,” I said quietly. "I believe I don't need an appointment."

He stammered something, but I was already walking past him toward the stairs. Greg's office was on the third floor. I'd only been there once, years ago, when he first showed me around and gently explained I didn't need to concern myself with pack business. "Just be happy," he'd said, kissing my forehead. "That's your only job."

I climbed the stairs slowly, taking a whiff of a faint and sweet feminine scent. And I'd enjoy it if the thought of whose it might be wasn't choking me.

My heart hammered against my ribs as I continued on the stairs and into the elevator to the top floor. I told myself it meant nothing. She'd been here for meetings, for discussions about the surrogacy arrangement.

That was all.

That should be all. But the closer I walked to his office, the stronger the scent, and the louder the breathless voices.

I reached his office door at the end of the hall and gently knocked on the door, hoping my wobbling knees wouldn't give way.

I heard a sharp intake of breath before a male voice breathlessly called outside. “The documents can wait. Leave them outside.”

I swallowed. “Greg, It's me.”

There was frantic rustling, the scrape of furniture, a soft feminine gasp that made my heart clenched so tightly for a moment I thought it'll burst open.

Greg muttered something I couldn't make out, and the female voice giggled nervously. I closed my eyes, counted to three, and pushed the door open.

All the resolve, shattering, my body trembling so hard I thought I might break into pieces.

Hailey was sitting on Greg's lap.

Her arms were around his neck, her hair disheveled, her blouse slightly askew. Greg's hands were on her waist, his own shirt wrinkled like someone had been pulling at it. They both froze, staring at me with wide eyes.

For a long moment, no one moved until Greg exhaled slowly and gently set Hailey down. He stood up, adjusting his collar and smoothing his shirt, his expression was of gentleness, concern even, as if I'd just walked in on him doing paperwork.

"Layla," he called softly, taking a step toward me. "What are you doing here? Is everything alright?"

I exhaled shakily, pinching my thighs to stop myself from breaking down. "I want a divorce."

Chapter 4
Greg's POV

For one terrifying moment, my mind went completely blank.

Divorce?

She said divorce…?

A divorce? After years of marriage?

The word echoed in my skull, refusing to settle, or make any sense. This was Layla, my Layla, the woman who loved me, who'd given up everything for me, who'd looked at me with those warm eyes for years and never once wavered. She couldn't mean it. She was angry, hurt, speaking from emotion rather than reason.

She couldn't possibly mean it.

Divorce? Like we were in the human world. It sounded strange to my eyes.

She knew my feelings inside out. She knew me like the back of her palms, from the moment I stumbled onto her doorstep years ago, wounded and desperate, and she'd taken me in without hesitation. When the pack turmoil had forced me into the human world, I never expected to find my fated mate there—a human, gentle and kind, with eyes that saw past my wolf to something worth saving. She'd nursed me back to health.

It felt like fate. Like we were meant to be together.

She couldn't just throw all of that away? All the years, the memories, the happiness. There was no way she'd be willing to do that

No way.

Layla knew I loved her, I loved everything about her. Her eyes when she laughed, her smile first thing in the morning. The way she fit against me in bed, warm and trusting and completely mine.

But the pack was traditional. The elders had never accepted a human Luna, and  I'd fought them, withstood immense pressure to bring her here and mate with her. Yet the one problem I couldn't solve was the one that mattered most: she couldn't conceive. Three years of trying, of treatments, of hope crumbling into despair month after month, of the council members on my neck and the pack member baring their fangs at me.

When I chose Hailey as a surrogate, I'd briefly remembered my promise to Layla. But this wasn't cheating—this was the solution, this would ease Layla's guilt over her infertility and give me the heir the pack demanded. Everyone said she was only human, far too weak to carry werewolf children. There was no other way.

So why was she looking at me like that? Like I was a stranger. Like everything we'd built meant nothing.

"I'm not accepting this," I said, stepping forward as she turned to leave. My hand caught her wrist, stopping her. "You're just upset Layla, we've talked about it. You're not thinking clearly.”

Layla whirled back, and the fury in her eyes made me flinch. "I'm thinking more clearly than I have in years. You broke your promise, Greg. You cheated. And I won't stay married to a man who cheats."

"I wasn't cheating—"

"Then what is it?" She pulled her wrist free, stepping back. "You found another woman and you got her pregnant. At the same time frolicking with her behind my back and being shameless about it, what would you call that?"

Hailey stepped forward quickly, her expression soft and concerned. "Luna, please, don't blame Greg. He was only trying to do what's best for the pack. I know this is hard for you, but—"

"Don't." My voice came out as a snarl, cutting her off. Her attempts to calm her are only going to make it worse.

My eyes were fixed on Layla, on the woman I loved. "Layla, please. I love you. I've always loved you and you know that, it'll never change."

She chuckled, grinding her teeth. "Your love is selfish Greg. If you truly loved me, you would never have chosen a woman who's in love with you to be your surrogate. You would not have her  straddling you, you wouldn't be shameless about it, you wouldn't stand there and watch your pack slander me. Insult me, call me all sorts of names and compare me, compare me with your concubine and what? You want me to just... accept it? Be grateful?”

I fell silent, staring at her. At the deep frown lines on her forehead, she was almost baring her teeth at me, furious and fierce and nothing like the gentle woman who'd clung to me every night.

Did I make a mistake?

I quickly pushed the thought away. This was the only solution. Having an heir was too important and she would see that eventually.

When I snapped back to myself, Layla was gone, leaving the door wide open behind her as her footsteps faded down the corridor.

"Greg." Hailey's called as she  stepped closer, reaching for my arm. "She'll calm down. Give her time. I know this is hard, but—"

I shoved her away.

Her sympathy was the last thing I needed at the moment.

Hailey She stumbled back, catching herself against the desk, one hand flying to her stomach protectively.

"Greg," she breathed, eyes wide with hurt. "I know you're angry right now but I need you to understand that I'm carrying your heir."

I massaged my temple, hoping to calm my throbbing head and the pulsing ache behind my eyes that wouldn't stop. "Beta!"

He appeared almost instantly. "Yes, Alpha?"

"Escort Hailey out.." I turned to Hailey, trying to ignore the hurt on her face. "I've warned you before, you get compensated for your services which you'll focus on offering, nothing more. Don't step out of line."

“Of course, Alpha. I only want what's best." She  bowed slightly and followed the beta out, but at the door she glanced back, a malicious glint in her gaze.

I sank into a chair, rubbing my temples, trying to ignore the pain.

Beta returned moments later, hovering uncertainly. "Alpha? Hailey has been escorted safely."

"Good. Leave."

He hesitated. "Alpha... forgive me for asking, but... are you not afraid Luna will truly return to the human world?"

I looked up sharply. "What?"

"The way she looked when she left. I've never seen her like that. She seemed..." He trailed off.

I shook my head, certain despite the doubt gnawing at my edges. "She's angry but she loves me. She'll have to back down on this. Where would she even go? She has nothing there anymore."

An heir is too important.

And Layla knows that, so whatever this tantrum is needs to stop. Hailey was pregnant now and FLs petty jealousy could put the child in danger.

Once things settle, I'll coax her back. Buy her gifts, take her somewhere nice. She'll be obedient again.

She'll see how sincere I am with all this, and she'll trust me again.

Layla always comes around. This was probably just a stunt to piss me off. Layla was sensible enough to know how important this is to everybody.

"You said you would never leave me, Layla..."

~

Layla's POV

I trembled all over as I stumbled down the stairs, my legs barely supporting me when I felt bile rise up my throat, a quick wave of nausea hitting without warning, I rushed to the nearest potted plant and gagged, trying to throw up but nothing came up. Just dry, wrenching spasms that left me shaking and weak.

Day by day the nausea just seemed to grow worse.

Did I eat something bad?

Was the entire thing giving me an unsettling stomach? I doubted that.

I forced myself to keep moving, down the last floor, out the building's side entrance to where the car was parked, Bestfriend  spotted me immediately, jumping out and rushing over.

"Hey, hey, what happened? You look terrible..." She guided me into the backseat where Bestfriend  asked in concern.

I collapsed against the leather, grateful to be off my feet. Her younger brother Bestf. brother sat in the driver's seat, watching me with concern from the rearview mirror.

Bestfriend climbed in beside me. "Talk to me. What did he say? What happened up there?"

I told her everything, except I left out the part where I felt like I was going to die. "He doesn't get it," I finished, my voice cracking. "He actually thinks I'll just... He never gets it. He'll never.”

Bestfriend 's face hardened with fury, her fingers turning into a fist by her side. "That bastard! After everything you've sacrificed for him, everything you've given up—" She cut herself off, taking a breath. "You're doing the right thing. Don't let him sweet-talk you back, you're better off without a man like that, he's sooner or later going to break your heart, more than he's done today.

Bestf. brother spoke up from the front seat, glancing back and forth through the rearview mirror and back at the road. "The pack's security is tight at all official exits, but there's a secret path that'll take you there. Younger wolves use it to sneak out to human territory sometimes. The elders don't know about it—or pretend not to." He glanced back at me. "I can show you.”

I glanced at Bestfriend  who nodded. “Yeah, I told him about it.” she replied. “We'll be out of here soon, out of her and out of his life. With all the gossip flying around he still doesn't even care about you? Did he not see how tired and sick you look? Why then? “You're better off without him.” She added.

I thanked her softly and gave my buzzing phone my attention. I swiped down to the notification to see a missed call from OB-GYN. I glanced at Bestfriend , hoping this wouldn't be another bad news to make my day worse than it already is.

Chapter 5
Layla's POV

The OB-GYN’s voice on the phone was warm, almost cheerful. "Good news about your health, Layla. Nothing to worry about at all. I'm not much for texting these things—old-fashioned, I know—so I'll send a physical letter to your home. Check your mail when you can."

I thanked OB-GYN, hung up, and immediately pressed a hand to my churning stomach. The nausea hadn't let up, rolling through me in waves that left me breathless. Probably Hailey's perfume. That cloying scent had probably soaked into every surface of the pack house by now, poisoning everything it touched.

Bestfriend  watched me from across the car, concern etched on her face. "You've been sick for weeks now. The nausea, the exhaustion..." She hesitated. "Layla, is it possible you're pregnant?"

A hollow laugh escaped me before I could stop it. "Pregnant?."

That's impossible.

"I'm just saying, the symptoms—"

"I took a test yesterday, and a million other times, Bestfriend ." I turned to her. "I even took a test the day before and it came out negative. The same negative I've seen dozens of times over three years of trying." I shook my head, turning away.

Humans rarely conceive werewolf children, it was an impossibility Greg was willing to risk his life and title for. An impossibility she thought she could cross over. She couldn't possibly be pregnant.

Any woman would feel sick to the stomach inhaling the scent of her husband's lover. It's no brainer.

Bestfriend  squeezed my hand but said nothing. What was there to say?

My phone buzzed again. I glanced down, frowning at the unknown number flooding my screen with messages, my notifications vibrating. I picked up the phone and swiped it open, tapping on one of the notifications.

It was a dozen of photos from an unknown number, I tapped on the bunch and waited for it to load and when it did.

I wished I hadn't.

There were photos of Greg and Hailey in  positions so intimate I felt all traces of air leaving my lungs. Their faces so close together, laughing at something outside the frame.

He wouldn't be laughing so hard in another woman's arms if she was nothing but a surrogate to him.

Another photo was Hailey's hand on Greg's chest, looking up at him with adoring eyes, there were many other similar ones, many other incriBestfriend ting photos, evidence, that Greg had not only betrayed her trust but he so heartily insulted her to her face by lying, refusing to admit the truth.

Another photo was of Greg's arm around Hailey's waist, guiding her through the pack's private gardens.

Is that what the baby wanted? For his mother to  walk around the park like a Disney princess with a mate that wasn't hers.

Another was a selfie of Hailey in Greg's office, pouty smile directed at the camera while Greg's blurred figure worked at his desk in the background.

Hailey in a silk robe, lounging on a bed I didn't recognize, captioned: He says I'm beautiful in the mornings.

Hailey?

She sent these?

The messages kept coming, along with pictures to prove their credibility.

You really thought he loved you? Who would actually love a barren human? So sweetie I hope you stop being delusional and let him rest.

I stared at Greg's face in those photos, he looked relaxed, happy, at ease with another woman.

Maybe he'd never really been mine at all. I was a barren human after all.

“I'm leaving.” My voice sounded distant, even I couldn't fully hear it. “If you don't mind Bestfriend  Tonight, I'll sleep over, wake up as early as I can tomorrow morning and go pack my things."

I lost the one person I left my whole life for. The one person that was my entire world.

Bestfriend  nodded firmly. "Rest assured sweetie. We'll get you out of this hellhole.”

That evening, we confirmed the escape route Bestf. brother knew about, he even had a tiny map of it. Once we were sure of the plan we returned to Bestfriend 's place.

I lay on her spare bed, staring at the ceiling. As my phone buzzed and vibrated continuously from Greg neverending texts. He had been texting all night. And I had no will to look at any of them, afraid If I saw his words —which I hope was a desperate explanation, a sensible one that overrides those pictures —I might lose the will to go.

But I can't stay here any longer, suffering day by day hoping it'll get better when it only grows worse.

No one even appreciated my presence here, it's so obvious I matter less, to everyone. And to him.

Once I leave here, I'd go back to being that perfect woman. In a world where I'm seen as equal and people appreciate everything you do.

In a world with people like me, a world where I won't get judged for joy being able to conceive an heir for the Alpha.

I'd be free and happy…

I closed my eyes, willing myself to see where I'd be. I saw myself in a sharp blazer, striding through glass-and-steel hallways, confident and capable. I heard my own voice presenting strategies to rooms full of executives who actually listened. I felt the satisfaction of a campaign that exceeded every target, the pride of building something with my own hands.

When had I last felt that? When had I last been someone who mattered for who I was, not whose wife I was?

The werewolf world had taken so much from me. My career, my independence, my sense of self. In return, it had given me love, or what I'd thought was love, that required me to shrink to the smallest I can ever go, to sacrifice, to accept less than I deserved—was that really love at all?

Morning came almost too fast. I dressed in yesterday's clothes, borrowed a toothbrush from Bestfriend , and prepared myself for the hardest walk of my life.

"You want me to come?" Bestfriend  asked.

"No. This I do alone." I squeezed her hand. "Thank you, best."

Bestf. brother drove me to the pack house and parked a block away. "I'll wait here. Don't take too long—the longer you're inside, the less time we have."

I nodded, squared my shoulders, and walked toward the home I'd shared with Greg for these past few years.

The front door was unlocked when I got in. I stepped inside the foyer—and stopped dead in my tracks at the sight before me.

Hailey sat on my couch, in my living room, feet propped on my coffee table like she owned the place. She was eating grapes from a fruit bowl, scrolling through her phone, utterly at home.

She looked up and smiled when she saw me. Triumphantly. "Oh, you're back. I was starting to think you'd done the smart thing and left already. What a shame."

I shook my head. What was I thinking, hoping Greg would give me a reason to not leave? "Get out of my house."

"Your house?" She laughed, light and cruel. "Sweetheart, nothing here is yours. The house belongs to the pack. The Alpha belongs to the pack. Even that pathetic little dress you have on, I'll give you that. Take it and go."

I forced myself to breathe. "You're pregnant, Hailey, and I'm trying to remember that, to be civil. But you need to leave. Now. I want you out of my house."

Hailey rose gracefully, one hand resting on her flat stomach. "You know, I almost feel sorry for you. Almost. All those years trying to be something you're not, trying to fit into a world that was never meant for you. Did you really think someone like him could ever truly love someone like you?"

"Don't." My voice dropped low. "Don't you dare talk to me about love."

"I know he came to me." She stepped closer, smile widening. "I know he chose me to carry his child. I know he spends his nights with me now, not with you. When the elders demanded an heir, he didn't fight for you—he came running to me. That's your great love Layla, isn't it? How are you this delusional?”

My hands clenched. "You're carrying a child he created behind my back, scared that he'll lose me when he finds out. That's not love, that's betrayal, that's fear, that tells you more than you want to admit. And if you think he'll treat you any differently, you're the delusional one."

Hailey's eyes flashed with anger. "I'm not you! I'm pure-blood, I'm everything you're not and will never be” She poked my chest. “I can give him things you never will Layla, allies, status, children name it! But you're nothing, you've always been nothing and just so you know he only kept you out of pity."

"And yet here you are," I said quietly, "in my house, trying to convince yourself you've won. If you were so sure of his love, you wouldn't need my validation, you don't have to parade around the entire pack with your stomach out seeking one, it shows how unloved and desperate you are. You don't even have a mate, you can't keep one, so what you do is go around, sleeping with every man you know. Look at a surrogate, standing up to the wife, something you'll never be. So much for a pure blood."

“You think you're better than me? You barren wench!! He'll forget you existed within a month. Our child will call me mother, and you'll be nothing but a sad story—the obsessed human who couldn't let go."

"Well, until then. Get out."

"Or what?" She laughed again, stepping closer, invading my space. "Go ahead, send me out yourself. One little touch and you'll be responsible for harming the pack's heir. Come on, do it, prove to me you're strong enough and see who wins."

"You're crazy, Hailey, and I have no time to deal with a crazy, man obsessed slut."

She wants it? She can have it. Greg was never mine to begin with. He found the person he wanted, the woman he's left me for. Well, they can have each other. I just want to be done with this. “You can have my leftovers…”

Hailey's face contorted. "How dare you call the alpha a leftover—"

"How dare I?" I stepped forward, and she stepped back, fear flickering in her eyes. "How dare I? What? You don't want him anymore now that you realize he's a leftover? He's a man I'm going to leave, what else is he if not a leftover?”

She opened her mouth, but no words came. For one moment, she was speechless and I hoped and thought it'll remain that way, until she stumbled backward, falling to the floor, and let out a piercing scream.

"What are you doing?" I started toward her, but she let out another scream, clutching her stomach.

“Please Luna, don't hurt me! Please, the baby—! He did nothing wrong to you!”

The front door slammed open almost immediately, Greg rushing in like he was on fire. He stopped in front of us, taking in the scene, he rushed to Hailey’s aid, helping her up before he turned to me, livid. His eyes a shade I've never seen before..

"What the hell are you doing?!" He snarled. "FL—what did you do?"

Chapter 6
Layla's POV

I stared at him, unable to form the right words. He didn't believe me. After everything, after years of marriage, after all the love I'd given him, he stood there holding another woman and looked at me like I was the liar, the villain, the one who had done something wrong.

Hailey whimpered against his chest, pathetically, and then her body went limp. She crumpled gracefully, sliding toward the floor in a performance so dramatic it would have been comical under different circumstances. Greg caught her instantly, panic flashing across his face as he eased her onto the couch, checking her pulse, her breathing, pressing gentle fingers to her stomach where his precious heir grew.

I watched from where I stood.

When he was satisfied she was breathing, when the initial fear subsided, he turned to me. His eyes were hard, cold, nothing like the man who had held me just weeks ago and whispered that he loved me.

"I know you're hurt," he said, sounding hurt like he was the one pregnant and allegedly abused. "I know you're angry. I've tried to be patient with you, tried to understand, tried to give you space to process everything. But this time you've gone too far. You know how badly the pack needs an heir. You know the pressure I've been under from the elders, from everyone. That child she's carrying is my only heir, FL! The only chance I have to satisfy them and secure my position, and you—"

"Your only heir." It was almost funny I chuckled. Watching him act like a hero for his concubine. "That child is a bastard. Born outside our marriage. Conceived behind my back while I was taking fertility treatments, while I was begging doctors to help me give you what you wanted. And you stand there and call it your only heir."

His jaw tightened. "You know what I mean."

"I know exactly what you mean." I set my  trembling hands down to my sides, I needed them to stop shaking. "That child has noble blood. Pure werewolf lineage. An alpha's daughter for a mother. That makes it legitimate in their eyes, doesn't it? More legitimate than anything I could ever give you. More legitimate than me even, our marriage, the years we spent together."

"That's not what I said."

"It's exactly what you said, Greg." My voice stayed calm all the days of practice paying off, hiding the slow burning realization spreading through my chest like fire. "I'm your Luna. Your wife. Your mate! We've been married for years. And yet you stand there, in front of me, holding another woman, and call her child your only heir. What does that make me, Greg? What have I been to you all these years?"

He opened his mouth but no words came out. I saw everything I'd been too blind to see before. The way he'd never introduced me as his Luna at pack gatherings, only as my mate. He'd gently discouraged me from taking on pack duties, telling me I didn't need to concern myself with such things. The way he'd isolated me from pack life while simultaneously complaining about the elders' pressure. He made me feel everything a wife wasn't supposed to feel.

Something in my stomach twisted, a dull persistent ache that had nothing to do with emotion. I pressed a hand to my abdomen, willing it to pass.

Greg noticed. For just a split second, something flickered in his eyes—concern, maybe, or some buried instinct that remembered he'd once loved me. His body tensed like he might step toward me.

Then Hailey moaned softly on the couch, and the moment shattered.

His expression hardened. "I already warned Hailey once for your sake. I told her to keep her distance, to stay out of our way. I did that for you. I've been fair to you. But you need to understand that there are things bigger than your feelings right now. The pack needs this heir. I need this heir. And you—" He stopped, shook his head. "You need to go upstairs. Now. Stay in our room until I decide what to do with you."

I stared at him. "What?"

This is ridiculous.

"I can't have you running around the pack, spreading stories, causing scenes. The elders are already watching, already waiting for me to slip up. If word gets out that my Luna attacked a pregnant woman—"

"I didn't attack her."

"It doesn't matter what actually happened!" He yelled, like he was explaining something to a child who couldn't understand. "It matters what people believe. And right now she's weak on my couch and you're standing there glaring at her. How do you think that looks?"

"Like you cheated on me and I finally grew a spine?" I took a deep breath. "I don't care how it looks, Greg, I'm done. I want a divorce. I'm going upstairs to grab my stuff, and I'm leaving."

I turned toward the stairs but he  moved faster than I could track. One moment he was across the room, the next his hand clamped around my wrist, so hard it began to hurt.

"You're not going anywhere."

I tried to pull free but his grip only tightened. "Let go of me."

"Not until you listen to reason." His voice softened slightly, the old Greg peeking through, the one who used to hold me gently and promise forever. "I love you. You know I love you. I'm doing this for us, for our future Layla. Once the heir is born, once the elders are satisfied, we can go back to how things were. You and me, just like before."

"There is no before." I pulled against his grip, my wrist aching. "There is no going back. You slept with another woman, you frolicked around with her, you got her pregnant, and you were never apologetic about it, always blaming me, always taking her side like I don't matter. What else do you want from me?! I'm done, Greg! I'm done!"

"Will you listen to me?!!." He stepped closer, his eyes searching my face desperately. "You're not thinking clearly. I know you're emotional, you're hurt, you're making decisions you'll regret. Just give it time, a few days, a week, and you'll see I'm right. You'll see that everything I do is because of the both of us. I'm giving this union my all and you're not going to throw that away just because you're jealous."

Jealous?

Jealous?!!

I was jealous?

I looked past the handsome face and the desperate eyes and the familiar features I'd loved for so long. And underneath all of it, I finally saw how far I've come with my delusions. Hailey was right. I was delusional.

"This shows just how much you don't respect me." My voice came out as a whisper. "You never have, and I don't think you ever will."

His face went pale. "That's not true."

title: 🗣️💔 "Let's divorce." Cold words, freedom sought.
body:
After I caught my husband Clark having an affair with his secretary in the office, I filed for divorce. Unexpectedly, the only condition he proposed was to sleep with him...
**
"Nyla, are you sure you want me to draft a divorce agreement?" Valarie's voice crackled through the phone, hesitant and worried. "Think about it. Once you sign this, you and Clark will have nothing to do with each other anymore."
 
Nyla stared at the amber liquid in her glass. The whiskey burned her throat, but nothing could burn away the images from last night. Her fingers tightened around the phone.
 
"Yes," she said finally. "I'm leaving him."
 
"Why?" Valarie's confusion bled through the speaker. "Clark's been so good to you. He loves you so much..."
 
Nyla almost laughed. Love. What a joke. She pressed her lips together, fighting back the bitter taste rising in her throat.
 
After hanging up, Nyla looked out the window. The massive LED screen on the skyscraper across the street was still playing that press conference. Clark stood there in his perfect suit, holding up that ridiculous jewelry piece.
 
Using the world's finest diamonds and gemstones, he had created a one-of-a-kind piece for his wife.
 
It was named "Love Nyla."
 
He named it after Nyla, declaring to the world his eternal love for her. Upon its release, "Love Nyla" instantly ignited social media discussion, remaining a hot topic.
 
The world was buzzing about their enviable love.
 
Outside, the LED screens continued to replay the video, but Nyla chuckled self-deprecatingly.
 
"Love me?" she muttered to herself. "Love me enough to sleep with another woman on our anniversary night?"
 
Last night was their third wedding anniversary. Clark had said he wanted to surprise her and asked her to wait for him at home. Nyla wore Clark's favorite white dress, lit candles, and prepared his favorite dinner, waiting eagerly until late at night.
 
She had waited. And waited. Midnight came and went.
 
At one in the morning, her phone suddenly buzzed with a Facebook friend request. A strange profile picture with the note "A surprise for you."
 
Nyla was about to reject the message outright, but then the person sent another message: [Are you still awake? Is it because your husband isn't with you?]
 
Nyla's alarm bells went off. How did this person know Clark wasn't home? She didn't accept the friend request, but the messages kept coming: [Stop pretending, I know you're reading this.]
 
[Your husband is with me now.]
 
[I was scared of thunder, so he worried about me and came to keep me company.]
 
[What a good man, but it's a shame he's not good for you alone.]
 
Each message stabbed Nyla like a knife in the heart. Her hands trembled. Her mind told her it might be a prank, but deep down, a voice frantically questioned it.
 
The last message completely broke her defenses: [If you don't believe me, I'll send you the address. The door lock code is your wedding anniversary.]
 
Nyla couldn't sit still any longer. With trembling fingers, she accepted the friend request. The other party immediately sent an address and a password: 0823. It was indeed their anniversary.
 
Nyla rushed out of the house like a madman and drove to the address. It was an upscale apartment. She stood in front of the door, her finger hovering over the combination lock, her heart pounding.
 
She entered 0823, and the lock clicked and the door opened.
 
A men's suit jacket lay scattered in the hallway. She recognized it as the three-year anniversary gift she had given Clark, which Clark had worn when he left that morning.
 
A pair of black lace paanties lay on the sofa in the living room, and a wine glass with a woman's lipstick stain on it lay on the coffee table.
 
From the hallway to the bedroom, men's and women's clothing was scattered everywhere. The most striking thing was a red lace nightgown, torn to shreds, lying by the bedroom door.
 
Nyla's legs were so weak she could barely stand, but she still trembled as she pushed open the half-open bedroom door. On the bed, Clark, na-ked, embraced another woman. The woman knelt on the bed, her head buried between Clark's legs, licking Clark's pen.is.
 
Clark's eyes were closed, his face a look of enjoyment, m0-aning, "Yes, that's it, great..."
 
The woman asked proudly, "Am I better, or is Nyla better?"

Clark stood frozen for several seconds, torn between answering the phone and staying with his wife. Finally, he made his choice and headed for the door.
 
As he stepped into the hallway, Nyla could hear his voice through the thin walls: "Jordyn, what's wrong? Are you feeling sick? I'll be right there..."
 
His voice faded as he moved further away, leaving Nyla alone in their living room.
 
The silence felt suffocating. Nyla stared at the white walls, feeling like they were closing in on her.
 
Twenty minutes after Clark left, Nyla's phone buzzed with an incoming call. She didn't recognize the number, but she answered anyway.
 
"Mrs. Summer, I hope I'm not interrupting," came Jordyn's sweet voice. "I'm not feeling well, so I borrowed Clark from you tonight. He came without hesitation when I called. He said nothing was more important than making sure I was okay."
 
Nyla's grip tightened on the phone, but she said nothing.
 
Jordyn continued with obvious satisfaction. "You know what Clark told me today? He said I'm younger and prettier than you. He said I can give him something you never could - a child. He mentioned that you haven't been able to conceive in three years. He's worried there might be something wrong with your body."
 
"Oh, and that strawberry mousse cake you threw away today?" Jordyn's voice turned mocking. "Clark buys me that same cake all the time. He says sweet treats are perfect for sweet girls. Don't you think it tastes sweet, Mrs. Summer?"
 
The call ended with Jordyn's cruel laughter.
 
Nyla sat in the darkness, feeling something fundamental shift inside her. The pain was so intense it took her breath away. Then slowly, mercifully, numbness began to set in.
 
From that day forward, Nyla began quietly packing her belongings. She folded her clothes carefully and placed them in suitcases.
 
She packed her books, her makeup, her jewelry. Each item felt heavy with memories she no longer wanted to keep.
 
Clark became even busier during this time. He came home later and later, sometimes not at all. When he did return, he was distant and distracted.
 
Meanwhile, Jordyn's messages never stopped. Photos of her growing belly, pictures of expensive gifts, taunting words designed to twist the knife deeper.
 
Nyla's best friend Valarie came over to help with the divorce paperwork.
 
"Given that Clark committed adultery and got another woman pre-gnant, you could definitely ask for substantial compensation," Valarie said seriously. "Plus, you gave up your career for this marriage. That's worth a lot in court."
 
Valarie spread the legal documents across the coffee table. "You sacrificed your research position at the university. You could have been earning six figures by now."
 
But before proceeding with anything official, Nyla felt she should tell her father. She drove to the hospital where he was still recovering from his recent surgery.
 
Her father looked better than he had in weeks. His color was returning, and he was sitting up reading the newspaper.
 
"Dad," Nyla began carefully, "if... hypothetically... if I wanted to get divorced, what would you think?"
 
Her father set down his newspaper and studied his daughter's face intently. "Nyla, is something wrong between you and Clark?"
 
Nyla forced herself to maintain eye contact. "I'm just curious. If that day ever came..."
 
"Absolutely not!" Her father's voice rose sharply. "Nyla, do you understand what the Summer family has done for us? When my factory had that terrible accident, they provided the money that saved us from bankruptcy. They've been paying my medical bills for three years. Without them, we would have lost everything."
 
Her father's face was flushed with emotion. "Clark has been nothing but good to you. How could you even think such thoughts? Has someone been filling your head with ideas?"
 
Nyla realized she couldn't continue this conversation. Her father had no idea about Clark's betrayal. She couldn't bear to put her sick father through that kind of shock and disappointment.
 
She was about to change the subject when her father's phone chimed with a text message. He glanced at the screen and his face went completely white.
 
The message was from Jordyn. It contained a photo of her and Clark kissing passionately in what looked like a hotel room.
 
Below the image was a message that read: "Thought you should know - I'm pre-gnant with your son-in-law Clark's baby."

 
Chapter 8
 
Harrison suddenly developed a violent coughing fit. His body convulsed as he struggled to breathe.
 
His face turned an alarming shade of blue, and his hands clawed at his chest. The phone slipped from his trembling fingers and clattered to the floor.
 
Nyla saw the message on the fallen phone and immediately understood what had triggered his condition.
 
Rage flooded through her veins, but her father's health took priority over confronting Jordyn. She frantically pressed the call button for the nurses.
 
"Help! I need a doctor now!" she shouted into the hallway.
 
A team of medical staff rushed into the room. They immediately began checking her father's vital signs while Nyla stood helplessly in the corner, watching his condition deteriorate before her eyes.
 
The lead doctor emerged from the examination looking grave. He pulled off his mask and shook his head slowly.
 
"Mr. Jayston's condition has suddenly worsened," he said wearily. "His kid ney failure has progressed rapidly. We need to transfer him to the ICU immediately for intensive monitoring and treatment."
 
Nyla felt her legs go weak. "How serious is this?"
 
"It's critical," the doctor replied bluntly. "But I'm afraid we have a problem. Our ICU is completely full. Every bed is occupied, and there's a waiting list. All the hospitals in the city are experiencing the same shortage of resources."
 
"Wait?" Nyla could barely comprehend what she was hearing. "Doctor, my father can't wait. Look at him!"
 
Her father was still struggling to breathe normally. His skin had a grayish pallor that terrified her.
 
"I understand your concern, Mrs. Summer, but we're doing everything we can," the doctor said helplessly. "All we can do right now is stabilize his condition with medication and hope a bed opens up soon."
 
Desperation clawed at Nyla's chest. She thought immediately of Clark. As the heir to Summer Group, he had connections throughout the medical community. He could pull strings and get her father the care he needed.
 
With shaking hands, she dialed Clark's number.
 
After several rings, someone picked up. But it wasn't Clark's voice that greeted her.
 
"Hello, who's calling?" came Jordyn's sickeningly sweet voice.
 
Nyla's blood turned to ice. "This is Nyla. I need to speak to Clark immediately. It's an emergency."
 
"Oh, Mrs. Summer!" Jordyn's voice was dripping with false concern. "Clark is in the shower right now. He's been taking such good care of me all day that he's completely exhausted. Poor thing needs to rest."
 
Nyla bit back her fury and forced herself to stay focused. "This is about my father. He's dying and needs an ICU bed. Please put Clark on the phone right now."
 
"Oh my, what terrible timing," Jordyn said with obvious fake sympathy. "I wasn't feeling well this afternoon either. Just some pre-gnancy nausea and dizziness, you know how it is. But Clark was so worried about me and the baby that he immediately called in the best medical team in the city. They're all on standby right now, just in case something happens to us."
 
Nyla's hands were shaking so violently she could barely hold the phone. Her father was dying, and her husband was playing house with his pre-gnant mistress.
 
"Can you please just-" Nyla began, but Jordyn cut her off.
 
"Oh, I hear the shower turning off. Clark will be so tired after everything we've been through today. I should probably let him rest. You understand, don't you?"
 
The line went dead.
 
Nyla stood in the hospital hallway, feeling like the world was collapsing around her.
 
She closed her eyes and tried to think of alternatives. Then suddenly, an image flashed through her mind - a figure handing her a coat in the rain. Damon's cold but decisive voice echoing in the car.
 
Without allowing herself to second-guess the decision, she dialed his number.
 
"Mr. Damon, this is Nyla," she said when he answered. "I'm sorry to bother you, but my father is critically ill. He needs an ICU bed urgently, but the hospital says they don't have any available. I know this is a lot to ask..."
 
"Send me the hospital address," Damon's voice cut through her rambling. It was sharp and authoritative. "I'll handle it. Ten minutes."
 
The line went dead, but his words carried more reassurance than Clark's empty promises ever had.
 
Exactly ten minutes later, the hospital director personally arrived at her father's ward.
 
Behind him came a full medical team, including specialists Nyla recognized from medical journals. They moved with efficient precision.
 
"Mr. Jayston will be transferred to our premium ICU immediately," the director told Nyla respectfully. "We're bringing in the city's leading kid-ney specialists for consultation. He'll receive the absolute best care available."
 
Within an hour, her father was settled in a private ICU room with round-the-clock monitoring.
 
That evening, after her father's condition had finally stabilized, Nyla returned to the house she had shared with Clark.
 
She sat in their living room, surrounded by three years of memories that now felt like lies.
 
She opened her phone and began forwarding every single message and photo Jordyn had sent her to Clark's email address.
 
The videos of Jordyn showing off expensive jewelry. Photos of their intimate moments in the apartment Clark had bought her.
 
Recordings of Jordyn rubbing her belly and cooing, "Daddy loves us so much. He's going to give us everything."
 
After sending all these, Nyla typed a final message: "Clark, these are from your girlfriend Jordyn. Since you two love each other so much, I'll step aside and let you be together."
 
Then she photographed the divorce papers Valarie had prepared and attached them to another email: "The divorce agreement is ready. Have your lawyer contact Valarie tomorrow to finalize everything."
 
After hitting send, Nyla stood up and began dismantling their life together.
 
She pulled their wedding photos off the walls and threw them directly into the trash. The jewelry Clark had given her, the clothes he had bought, the makeup he had surprised her with - everything went into garbage bags.
 
She called a moving company and worked through the night to clear out her belongings. By dawn, the house looked exactly as it had before she had moved in - empty and cold.
 
Nyla took one final look around the space that had once felt like home.
 
She dragged her suitcase to the door and walked out without looking back.

title: 🔥Don’t pay a cent.✨ Read it all — free, free, free!✨🔥
body:
I, the princess of the Moretti Empire and the DeNucci family’s combined empire, became pregnant with the president of the Princes of Darkness MC., at the age of 21. 
But he betrayed and abandoned me. After that, I left his side and also distanced myself from my family. 
Just when I was about to live a peaceful life, a group of bikers surrounded me, and at the forefront was the man who had hurt me the most—Ryder Savage Jackson......

“Mommy … go.” I push the cart around the store as I watch my beautiful two-year-old daughter Rebel clap her hands as I go faster, and she squeals in delight.
 
She is so much like him. He who shall not be named kind of scenario. She doesn’t take after me much apart from the honey eyes. Her dark blonde hair and nose are like his and boy, does she have his temper.
 
“Ok Rebel, we need to finish this. Then we will go to the park. How does that sound?” she kicks her legs and claps again. I chuckle at her behaviour, leaning down to kiss her head. I finish off shopping and head out to the car.
 
I left home over three years ago. Three years I ran. The same man that is Rebel’s father hurt and humiliated me. I never got to tell him he was about to become a father. The woman he claimed had already done that. I couldn’t risk my parents finding out, either. It would have caused a war between my family and his MC.
 
My dad is the Don of the Moretti empire and my momma, well, she is the head of the cartel and the DeNucci family. I am their only daughter. The princess of the combined empire. My twin brother Nathaniel is next in-line to take the position of Don after dad retires and me well, I was supposed to take over the DeNucci family and my younger brother Nico would take over the cartel.
 
That all went to mess when I ran. It was difficult at first going to a new place. Living not just for myself but for the life I was carrying inside of me. The savings I had I used to find a place to live, get everything we needed and what was left, I invested it in a rundown bar.
 
I changed my name and never looked back. My bar is doing so well and it is nice to know that I have made it what it is today. The bar is called the Eclipse. The town we live in is a tourist town. So we get different people coming and going.
 
Most people come here to the lake in the summer and the skiing in the winter. It’s a friendly and safe place to live and I am happy here. When I first arrived here, I was lost, but I was welcomed and I wouldn’t leave even if you paid me too.
 
Once we have arrived at the house. It’s nothing like the Moretti mansion, but it’s home. With its white picket fence. White walls and blue door. It doesn’t look like much from the outside, but it’s open plan on the inside and modern. Upstairs there are three bedrooms, all with an en-suite and a family bathroom. Rebel has her own room next to mine and life is good.
 
She doesn’t want for anything; I carry the shopping inside and then carry Rebel in. Shutting the door, I place her in the living room with some of her toys as I put the shopping away. Just then, Boomer bounds inside. Rebel loves him as much as he loves her. I got Boomer when I was preqnant and both he and Rebel grew together.
 
He is a beautiful big softy. He is a Cane Corso. He is as black as night with a tiny patch of white on his tʃest. He is our protector, even if he does drool everywhere and talks back when you tell him no.
 
My phone rings and I take it out of my back pocket and see that it is Coral who is supposed to work the bar tonight. I gr0an, knowing she is about to ask me to cover her shift, no doubt because her douchebag ex won’t have their child tonight.
 
“Hey Coral, what’s up?”
 
“Hey Angie, look, I’m really sorry to do this, but Steve ditched me and I can’t find a sitter.” I roll my eyes. If I had a dollar for every time he has let her down over the last year, I would be a wealthy woman.
 
“Ok. Coral, no worries, but you and I need to have a chat about this. I will cover tonight, but you need to sort this out.” I hate being the bad guy, but she knows I have a toddler, too. I don’t have the support she does, even if it is my own doing.
 
“I will get it sorted. I’m so sorry Angie. I promise I will make it up to you.” We say goodbye and end the call. I look at Rebel and sigh. Still time to take the little miss to the park, and then I will have to call Mrs Lawson and see if she is available. I know she will be she loves Rebel.
 
“Boomer, leash.” I say and he is off to get what I’ve asked as I scoop up my now rowdy toddler and get her ready for the park.
 
“Go now?” I smile at her.
 
“Yes, sweetheart, we can go now.” I say, kissing her on her cheek. Grab the stroller and strap her in. Getting her in is always a workout. The child goes as stiff as a board and she finds it hilarious.
 
I make the call to Mrs Lawson as I put the leash on Boomer and pray she can help.
 
“Hello, Angie, how are my two favourite girls today?” I grab my keys and some snacks and drinks, placing them in the changing bag and attach it to the stroller.
 
“We are doing just fine. I hate to do this last minute, but Coral called and …”
 
“Say no more. I will be at your house at seven, then you can head out.” God love this woman. She is my lifeline.
 
“Thank you so much, I hate to spring it last minute.”
 
“Nonsense, sweetheart. You know I love to help out.”
 
“Thank you again, Mrs Lawson. I will see you soon.”
 
“How many times, call me Scar. You are family. No need to thank me. I will see you both soon. Bye Angie.” I hang up and head out.
 
After a couple of hours at the park and one tuckered out Rebel, she is fed and bathed and ready for bed. Mrs Lawson arrives and I head to work.
 
Pulling up at the bar, I notice we are packed out tonight. Well, at least the shift will go quickly.
 
Leaving the car, I head inside. I smile at some of the locals and make my way behind the bar. The night goes smoothly and begins to quiet down. I look at Max and tell him I’m going to office and if he needs me to come get me.
 
I head to the office to get some 0rders done and check the accounts and I lose track of time.
 
“Erm, Ang. I need you back at the bar.” I look up and smile as I stand and leave the office, shutting and locking the door behind me.
 
The music gets louder the closer I get to the bar. The sound of raucous laughter fills the air and something feels off. My gut twists and flutters the closer I get.
 
Stepping out behind the bar, I freeze. No, it can’t be. I notice the cuts.
 
The Princes of Darkness MC with white stitching against the black leather. An embroidered patch of a red devil with wings riding a Harley. The same MC that he runs, the very same MC that is in allegiance with my family. What are they doing this far out?
 
“Angel.” My eyes widen and my heart jumps into my throat as I look into the icy blue eyes of the man who broke my heart, the man who forked his wh0re in front of me, the man I ran from, the father of my daughter.
 
Ryder ‘Savage’ Jackson.

They have found me; they have found me. Crap, frick, tvat! I look at him and I’m having a mini panic attack. All I can see is him and her. The words he spewed at me with such hatred and the smirk on her face. Why is he here?

He reaches for me and I react instantly; I grip his wrist and turn him, shoving his arm up his back. He gr0ans and the men are now on their feet. I look at Blaze, his VP, and he is telling everyone to remain calm.

“You have the wrong person. Now get out.” I shove him forward as the fight-or-flight takes over. I need to get out of here. I need to leave. I need to grab Rebel and Boomer and go. But where?

“Angel, that’s not going to happen. We have been looking for you. Your family has been looking for you. We have found you and there is no running from us,” Savage says to me as I step back, my eyes not leaving his.

“My name isn’t Angel. I don’t even know who you are. Now I won’t ask again. Get the fudge out of my bar or we will have a problem.” My voice is like steel as I stare the fricker down. I won’t back down now. I have to protect my daughter.

I catch movement from the corner of my eye and hold my hand up, and the movement stops. 

Just then, the door opens and more bikers come in, surrounding me completely...
