title: Free All Chapters👉
body:
😭😭"Luna Allison, your pup…didn't survive. The hemorrhaging was severe, but we've stabilized you."
For a second, I didn't understand the words.
*Ally, our pup… our little one…*Jasmine's mournful voice resonated within me, my wolf's grief mirroring my own.
"I know," I whispered aloud. "I know, Jas." My lips barely moved. Even speaking felt like it might shatter me.
With trembling fingers, I reached for my phone on the bedside table.My Alpha mate, Lucian needed to know about our lost pup.
*He won't care, *Jasmine growled. *
"We still have to try," I murmured, dialing his number. The screen blurred—either from tears or the way my vision kept refusing to focus on reality.
One ring.
Two rings.
Three.
Each ring was a hammer to my ribs.
Finally, he picked up, but his voice was ice. "What is it, Allison?"
"Lucian, I'm in the hospital," I managed, my voice breaking. "I—"
He sighed. Not shocked. Not heartbroken. Just… annoyed. Like I'd interrupted something important. Like I'd spilled coffee on his schedule.
"I'm in a meeting," he cut me off sharply. "Don't disturb me unless it's important."
My fingers tightened around the phone until my knuckles ached. "But Lucian, our p—"
"Handle it yourself." The line went dead.
Two years of marriage, and this—this was the mate I'd tried to love?
My mind drifted back, to a time when I'd been so naive. I had secretly adored Lucian Storm since my student days—the most popular Alpha heir in our academy, my silent hero. 
After I'd been trapped in that dark, isolated storage room for twelve terrifying hours, it was his keen werewolf hearing that had caught my muffled cries. He found me and rescued me.
But I foolishly believed he noticed me. 
One day after that Alpha Victor Storm, Lucian's grandfather, had been severely injured in a rogue attack, and I, purely by chance, had been the one to find him and staunch his bleeding long enough for the pack healers to arrive. 
I’d foolishly said yes when his grandfather Alpha Victor forced him to take me as Chosen Luna, a repayment for me saving his life. 
But Lucian believed I was the obstacle, an unwanted entanglement, standing between him and the woman he actually wanted—Heidi Lawrence, his college sweetheart.
Our marriage happened only because his powerful grandfather demanded it as payment for my unintended heroism.
The bond between our wolves, between Fenrir and Jasmine, was too fragile—or maybe too rejected—for his wolf to ever truly feel mine. 
He saw me not as a partner, but as an inconvenience, a perpetual source of trouble. 
An hour later, I couldn't stand lying in bed any longer.
Despite the nurse's warnings to stay in bed, I carefully swung my legs over the edge, grimacing at the pain that radiated through my abdomen.
"I just need to use the bathroom," I told her when she gave me a disapproving look.
The bathroom was just around the corner, and I was almost there when familiar voices drifted from the patient rooms across the hall.
"Are you sure you're feeling better now? We can get a second opinion if you're not satisfied with what the doctor said."
I froze. 
Lucian's deep voice was unmistakable.
My pulse leapt.
It was the softness in him—reserved, apparently, for everyone but me.
"I'm fine, really." Heidi's voice came sweet and breathy. 
"Thank you for coming with me, Lucian. I just got so worried when I felt those cramps."
My throat tightened until swallowing felt impossible. My hands went cold. My fingertips tingled.
"I told you I'd be here for you, didn't I?" Lucian's voice lowered, intimate. "Whenever you need me."
He’d hung up on after I lost our child… and was comforting his ex in the same hospital.﻿
I somehow made it back to my room, collapsing onto the bed as my legs gave out. My hands shook as I wiped at my cheeks, but the tears kept coming. 
The dull ache in my abdomen flared with every breath, but it was nothing compared to the raw, splintering pain tearing through my soul.
*This isn't right, Ally, *Jasmine urged. *We are not lesser wolves. We deserve a mate who values the bond… who values us.*
"No more," I said.
Jasmine went still. *If he comes back?*
My heartbeat steadied. One. Two. Three.
"Then he'll learn," I whispered, "I'm not the Luna he can abandon. I'm the mate he should've feared losing."
*****
It's been three days since I was discharged and returned to the pack.No one asked how I was. No one checked in.
I was a glorified housekeeper.
But is that really who I am?
I sat at my desk and stared at my research notes from before my marriage. I had been working on promising studies in traditional herbal remedies that could benefit werewolf healing.My work had been promising enough that Professor Jenkins, my mentor and fellow Moonstone Pack member, had recruited me for his team despite my youth. 
It had been my passion, my purpose—until meeting Victor Storm had changed everything.
With trembling fingers, I reached for my phone and dialed a number I hadn't called in nearly two years.
"Allison? Is that really you?" Professor Jenkins' familiar voice brought tears to my eyes. 
"Hello, Professor," I managed, trying to keep my voice steady. "I hope I'm not disturbing you."
"Not at all! Gods, it's been ages and we all miss you. "
I swallowed hard. "I miss you guys too, and I'm calling to ask about that confidential three-year research project you mentioned earlier. Is it still going on?"
"The Silvermoon Initiative? Yes, it's entering its second phase now. Do you want to join?!"
"I want in," I said decisively.
"Allison," his voice turned serious, "are you absolutely certain? This isn't just about the research, is it? What about your position as Luna of the Storm Pack? What about Lucian?"
The mention of his name sent a sharp pain through my chest.
I had been so certain that with enough love and patience, I could fill the emptiness in his heart.
I had forgotten that a glass bottle with no bottom could never be filled, no matter how much you poured into it.
"Please, Professor. I need to come home to something that's truly mine."
"If you're sure, then yes, we would welcome you back. Your research was truly groundbreaking, Allison."
After ending the call, I began gathering my old research files, opening folders that had remained untouched since my marriage.
My eyelids grew heavy as I worked and eventually, I drifted to sleep right there at my desk.
Suddenly, Lucian's voice slurred from the doorway.The strong scent of whiskey and unfamiliar perfume hit my nostrils, making my wolf growl protectively.
*He reeks of her,* Jasmine snarled inside my mind. *Heidi's scent is all over him.*
When we arrived in our bedroom, I helped him sit on the edge of our California king bed.
But before I could speak, he pulled me into his arms, his lips finding mine in a hungry kiss.
 "Lucian—" I tried to pull away, but he pressed me against the wall, his hands roaming my body with unusual urgency. "Need you," he mumbled against my neck, his teeth grazing the sensitive skin there. "Need you now."
How dare he come to me after getting cozy with another she-wolf, like nothing ever happened?
I shoved him away with all my strength, fury blazing through me like wildfire. The crack of my hand across his face echoed in the quiet bedroom.
He stood there, stunned, the red imprint of my palm blooming on his cheek. 
"What the—" 
"We're done," I said, my voice deadly calm despite the inferno raging inside me.
"Allison, you're not making any sense." He reached for me again, his movements uncoordinated.
I stepped away, creating distance between us. "I want a divorce."
"A divorce?" he repeated slowly, as if testing the unfamiliar concept.
"Are you hard of hearing, or just that dense? I said we're getting divorced—should I spell it out slower for you?"
*****
Lucian's POV
The slap had sobered me somewhat, though my head still felt foggy from the whiskey. 
*Is she serious?* Fenrir growled within me, surprisingly disturbed by her declaration.
*She can't be,* I responded internally. *It's just another emotional outburst.*
She stood before me, chin raised, those amber eyes burning with a determination I hadn't seen in her for... had I ever seen it?
This was clearly a ploy for attention—some desperate attempt to make me chase her after what had just happened.
"A little late for that strategy, isn't it? We've been married for two years."
*She's serious,* Fenrir growled within me, surprisingly upset. *Our mate is leaving us.*
She is a perfect silent partner who kept my home running smoothly while I built our empire. 
This defiance was new, and I didn't care for it.
"Don't be dramatic," I said dismissively. "You've had a perfect life here."
"Perfect?" She let out a sharp, brittle laugh. "I've been nothing but a glorified housekeeper to you."
"I have responsibilities to the pack and the company. You know that.I can make it up to you." I tried to soften my tone.
"I don't need anything from you anymore," she whispered.
"Where will you go? How will you support yourself? You haven't worked in two years, Allison. You've been a housewife—and not even a particularly good one at that."
Allison had tried desperately to fulfill the role of Luna, despite the pack's thinly veiled contempt for her common origins.
My mother had made her life especially difficult, constantly criticizing everything from her table manners to her inability to throw the lavish social gatherings expected of a Storm Pack Luna.
"That's none of your concern," she replied.
"I'm doing you a favor, Lucian. Do you really want her to remain your mistress forever? Wouldn't it be easier if I just stepped aside?"
"Who?" I froze.
"Heidi Lawrence, your first love."
My blood ran cold. "How do you know about Heidi?"
She shook her head. "This pack has eyes everywhere, Lucian. Did you really think your little rendezvous would stay secret?" 
"Where were you the day I called you? Just tell me the truth."
"I already told you," I answered stiffly. "I was in meetings."
Allison's laugh was bitter, escalating until tears formed in her eyes. "You'll never know what you lost, Lucian. Never."
She shook off my hands and turned away, moving toward the closet to begin packing.
Fenrir stirred within me, restless. *"Don't let her go, " *he growled. *" Say something. Stop her."*
But my pride held me still.
I decided to change tactics. "What about your mother? Who will pay for her care if not me?"
She paused for a heartbeat, her back still to me. Then she resumed folding. "I'll find a way," she replied quietly.
"What way?" I countered. "The specialized facility, the round-the-clock nurses—do you have any idea what that costs? Where would a housewife like you get that kind of money? Without me, she'd be in some state facility within weeks."
She turned to face me, and the naked hatred in her eyes made something in me recoil. "You're despicable! I regret ever loving you, Lucian," she said, her voice like ice.
Once the last piece was tucked in, she snapped the zipper shut with a decisive click and lifted the suitcase from the floor.
As she passed by me, her voice dripped with venom: "And let me give you something to chew on before I go. You really think you've ever satisfied me?"
My breath caught.
Uh-oh！
" The nights I melted in your arms? They were an act. Lucian. You can't please a woman with that undersized equipment and your two-minute performance."
Fenrir howled in humiliation.
She tilted her head. "See how long she entertains you once your empire starts cracking."
Then she turned and walked out—no hesitation, no backward glance.
*Go after her!* Fenrir demanded. *She is ours. We cannot let her leave!*
But my pride held me rooted to the spot.
Was she trying to threaten me with divorce? Or was this some ploy to attract my attention?
*****
Allison's POV
I had made it out—actually walked away from the life I'd built for two years, from the man I thought would be my forever.
*We did the right thing,* Jasmine reassured me, her presence warm in my mind despite the chill of the late hour.
The street was deserted, not a single car passing by at this ungodly hour.
Of course—who would be driving around the outskirts of wolf territory at 1 AM? 
*Call Bella,* Jasmine suggested. *She's always there for us.*
With trembling fingers, I dialed her number. One ring, two rings...
"Ally? Do you have any idea what time it is?" Bella's voice was thick with sleep, but instantly concerned.
"Bella," I whispered, my voice cracking. "I left him. I left Lucian. I need... I need somewhere to go."
"I'm at the edge of—" I froze mid-sentence as headlights flared behind me, washing the road in sudden brightness.
A sleek black Bentley glided up from behind—Lucian's car. My heart stopped as it slowed beside me, and I instinctively stepped back into the shadows.
Had he come looking for me? Was he going to try to drag me back? Or perhaps… apologize?
But it didn't stop. Through the tinted windows, I could make out Lucian's profile, his phone pressed to his ear, looking straight ahead as if I were invisible.
A bitter smile crossed my lips. Even now, he couldn't see me.
"Ally? You there?" Bella's concerned voice pulled me back.
"Yeah, sorry. I'm at the northern boundary of Storm territory, near Crescent Road. Can you come get me?"
"Already grabbing my keys. Sit tight, I'll be there in fifteen minutes."
True to her word, Bella's bright red Jeep came bouncing down the road exactly fourteen minutes later. She threw open the passenger door and jumped out, enveloping me in a fierce hug before I could even speak.
"I'm so proud of you," she whispered fiercely into my hair. "So damn proud."
*****
Bella’s small, cozy apartment was a far cry from the Storm Pack mansion, but it was warm. 
Over tea, Bella asked what pushed me over the edge. 
“I was pregnant, Bella. Three months along. I never told him because he was always too busy. And that day… I lost the baby. Our baby. And when I needed him most, he was off with her.”
Bella's face transformed from shock to fury in seconds.
"It doesn't matter now," I said quietly. "It's over."
Then I pulled out my phone and showed her the email I'd received from Professor Jenkins. "I applied to the research program at Northridge University. They accepted me."
Bella's eyes widened. "That's amazing! When do you start?"
"In a month. I told them I needed time to... wrap things up here."
"Well," she said, clinking her mug against mine, "here's to new beginnings. To Allison Carter, version 2.0."
"To new beginnings," I echoed, hoping I sounded more confident than I felt.
*****
The next day.
"I have an appointment with Katherine Wells," I told the receptionist. "Allison Carter-Storm."
"Ms. Carter. Right this way."
Once we were both seated, she folded her hands and fixed me with a penetrating gaze. "So, you want to divorce Alpha Lucian Storm. That won't be a simple process."
"I'm aware," I said, meeting her eyes steadily. "But I'm prepared for whatever comes."
We talked a lot.
Then. "I'll have the preliminary divorce papers drafted by tomorrow," Katherine promised as she walked me to the door. "Once you approve them, we'll serve them to your husband."
"Thank you," I said sincerely. "For taking my case, and for not treating me like a naive little wolf in over her head."
"You're stronger than you give yourself credit for," she replied with a knowing smile. "Most she-wolves would've crumbled long before reaching this point with an Alpha like Storm."
As I rode the elevator down to the parking garage, I felt lighter than I had in years.
My phone rang just as I reached my car. Leo's name flashed across the screen. Lucian's Beta, his right-hand man and enforcer. Why would he be calling me?Did Lucian send him?
Jasmine growled softly in my mind. *I gnore him.*
And I did, setting the phone down. 
By the time I pulled away from Wells Legal Services,not even two minutes later, it lit up again—Lucian.

title: ❤️FREE🔥click to read👉
body:
The pain wakes me at 3 a.m.

Not the dull ache of exhaustion—I'm used to that shit. Not the sharp sting of a fresh bruise—I've got plenty of those too. This is different. This comes from *inside*, like something's trying to claw its way out through my bones.

I gasp, curling into a ball on the thin mattress. My spine cracks—*pop pop pop*—each vertebra shifting like dominoes falling in slow motion. The sound is wet, organic, *wrong*.

*Oh God. Oh fuck. What the hell is this?*

My shoulder blades burn like someone's pressed hot irons against them from the inside out. I bite down on my pillow to keep from screaming. Can't let them hear. Can't give them the satisfaction of knowing I'm in pain.

*Not on the last day. Don't you dare break on the last damn day.*

I force myself upright, every movement sending fresh waves of agony through my skeleton. The storage room—my "bedroom" for the past ten years—is pitch black except for the faint green shimmer of aurora borealis dancing outside the single small window. November 30th in Alaska means no sunrise, no sunset. Just endless night.

Just like my life in this fucking house.

I stumble to the window and press my forehead against the freezing glass, desperate for relief. My skin is burning. I don't need a thermometer to know I'm running a fever—at least 104, maybe higher. My hands shake as I grip the windowsill.

*Am I dying? Is this it? Ten years of hell just to die in a storage room the night before I'm supposed to be free?*

The thought makes me want to laugh. Or cry. Or both. Instead, I just stare at the wall calendar I've been maintaining for years. Red X's mark off each day like a prisoner counting down to freedom. Tomorrow's date is circled three times in sharpie: *December 1st*. My eighteenth birthday.

The day this nightmare finally ends.

The day I can finally leave this place and never look back.

"Just one more day," I whisper to my reflection. The girl staring back looks like death—dark circles under brown eyes, skin pale and waxy, deep golden curls matted with sweat. "You can make it one more day, Kara. You've survived worse."

But have I? This pain... it's not normal. What if I collapse before I can escape? What if they find me dead in here and just shrug, call it "natural causes," dump me in an unmarked grave somewhere?

*No*. I dig my nails into the wood so hard I feel splinters bite. *Don't you dare die in this room. Don't give those bastards that satisfaction*.

The aurora outside flickers, green light washing over the snow-covered grounds. For a moment, I'm pulled back—not to the storage room, but to another cold night. The coldest night of my life.

---

*Ten years ago. December 1st. My eighth birthday.*

*We'd been driving for hours, Dad's hands white-knuckled on the steering wheel, Mom crying quietly in the passenger seat. I sat in the back with my snow wolf plushie clutched to my chest, not understanding why we were leaving our apartment in the middle of the night, why Mom kept saying "I'm sorry, baby, I'm so sorry" over and over.*

*The Midnight Estate appeared through the snow like something from a nightmare. Massive. Dark. Surrounded by endless white wilderness.*

*"Kara," Dad said, pulling the car to a stop outside the iron gates. His voice was shaking. "Sweetheart, we need you to be brave."*

*"Are we visiting someone?" I asked.*

*Mom made a sound like a wounded animal.*

*Dad got out, came around to open my door. The cold hit me like a physical blow—I'd never felt cold like that before, the kind that bites through your jacket and into your bones.*

*He knelt in the snow, eye level with me. His eyes were red. He'd been crying too.*

*"We need you to stay here for a little while," he said.*

*"How long?"*

*"Just... just until we get some things sorted out. With work. And... and some other stuff."*

*"But it's my birthday," I whispered. "You said we'd have cake."*

*He pulled me into a hug so tight I could barely breathe. His whole body was shaking. "I know, baby. I know. I'm so sorry. We'll come back for you. Soon. I promise."*

*"Connor, we have to go," Mom said from the car, voice thick with tears. "They're—we can't—"*

*"I know!" Dad snapped, then immediately softened. "I know, Celeste. Just... give me a minute."*

*He pulled back, hands on my shoulders. "Listen to me, Kara. The people here, they're... they're family. Sort of. Your mom's brother's wife. She's agreed to let you stay."*

*"Why can't I stay with you?"*

*"Because—" His voice cracked. "Because Daddy made some mistakes, and now we have to fix them. But you'll be safe here. Okay? You'll be safe."*

*Safe. The word felt wrong even then.*

*Mom got out of the car, stumbling through the snow in her thin heels. She pressed my snow wolf into my arms. "Take care of yourself, baby," she sobbed. "Be good. Be brave. We love you so much."*

*"Mom—"*

*"We have to go," Dad said, and suddenly they were both back in the car. The engine revved.*

*"Wait!" I screamed. "Daddy! Mom! Don't leave me here!"*

*But they were already moving, taillights disappearing into the snow.*

*I stood there, eight years old, in the middle of an Alaskan winter night with a duffel bag and a stuffed wolf, screaming until my voice gave out. "Come back! Please come back!"*

*The gates opened behind me.*

*A woman stood there—tall, elegant, wrapped in a thick fur coat. Her face was beautiful and cold as the snow around us.*

*"Stop that screaming," she said. Not unkind, but not kind either. Just... tired. "You'll wake the children."*

*"My parents—"*

*"—are gone. And they're not coming back. Not tonight, at least." She looked at me for a long moment, something complicated flickering across her face. Pain, maybe. Or anger. "Your father is my... he's family. And family helps family. Even when—" She stopped herself. "Come inside before you freeze."*

*"But they said—"*

*"I know what they said." She turned away. "Bring your bag. From today on, you'll work to repay what your parents owe. Room and board aren't free."*

*I was eight years old. I didn't understand words like "debt" or "owe." I just understood that my parents had left me in the snow on my birthday, and this cold woman with green eyes was all I had left.*

*So I picked up my bag and followed her into the darkness of Midnight Estate.*

*I haven't left since.*

title: High Cortisol Is Destroying Your Testosterone
body:
That's Not a "Dad Bod." That's cortisol overdose crashing your testosterone. Take your shirt off right now and look in the mirror.

Really look.

That soft belly hanging over your waistband isn't just "getting older." Those saggy man boobs aren't just "a few extra pounds." Those skinny arms that can't fill out a t-shirt sleeve aren't "genetics." That's your testosterone crashing in real-time. And every day you ignore it, you lose more of what makes you a man.

Your Body Is Eating Itself Because Your Hormones Are Broken
Here's what no doctor will tell you straight: That soft, undefined physique that makes you look weak even when you're not overweight? It's not fat you can diet away. It's muscle you can't build anymore.

When your testosterone crashes and your cortisol stays elevated, your body enters a catabolic state. That means it breaks down muscle tissue for energy. You literally consume yourself from the inside out.

Meanwhile, every carb you eat gets stored as fat—especially around your belly and chest. You're simultaneously losing muscle mass, gaining stubborn fat, and looking softer and weaker every year.

That's why you can eat clean, train hard, and still look like crap. Your hormones are sabotaging you.

And the worst part? While your body is getting softer on the outside, it's getting weaker on the inside. Your energy is gone. Your drive is gone. Your edge is gone. You feel like you're running on fumes even when you do everything right.

That's not laziness. That's hormonal failure.

The 2024 Study That Exposed the Masculinity Crisis
Researchers at UCLA studied 2,400 men between ages 30-50. They ran comprehensive hormone panels on every single one. What they found was terrifying.

78% had clinically low testosterone (below 400 ng/dL). 91% had chronically elevated cortisol (levels that should only appear during acute stress). 63% showed the metabolic profile of men 20 years older.

These weren't sick men. These were "normal" guys living "normal" lives. They thought they just had a "dad bod." Their hormones were collapsing. And their bodies were failing because of it.

The lead researcher said something that should terrify every man reading this: "We're watching an entire generation of men lose their masculine vitality in real-time. Their bodies are biologically older than their chronological age. And it's accelerating."

title: Read next chapter👉🏻
body:
What would you do if the man you loved—your husband of many years—betrayed you with someone right under your nose? How would you burn with rage? How far would you go for revenge?

*****

As night settled in, I finally got a moment to breathe after tucking my daughter into bed. I grabbed my phone and started mindlessly scrolling through TikTok, letting the videos wash over me—until a street fashion livestream caught my eye.

I straightened up, suddenly alert. The camera had just shifted, but for a brief second, I could’ve sworn I saw someone I knew. My chest tightened, and my palms started to sweat as I gripped my phone. I glanced at the time—yep, it was a live stream happening right here in the city.

Panic surged through me.

I quickly exited TikTok and hit the video call button for my husband, Gavin Rhodes.

He was supposed to be on a three-day business trip in Darsen. But I could’ve sworn I just saw him—on that livestream—with another woman wrapped around him.

The phone rang... and rang... until he finally picked up.

His camera was a little shaky, but then his face came into view—handsome, smiling, calm.

“Hey, babe!” he greeted warmly.

“Where are you?” I asked, trying to keep my voice steady while my eyes scanned the background behind him. He looked like he was in the hallway of a restaurant, dressed in a white shirt and tie. But the man from the livestream had been wearing a gray windbreaker.

“I’m at dinner with a client,” he said smoothly. “I stepped out to take your call. What’s up? Everything okay? Is Macy asleep?”

“Are you in Darsen?” I asked, dodging his question.

“Of course I am. Why?” His expression didn’t change. He just looked at me with mild curiosity.

“Oh. It's... nothing,” I mumbled, trying to sound casual. “When are you coming home?”

“Soon... I’ll wrap things up here and head back. You miss me already?” He smiled, full of affection. “I’ll try to be back as soon as I can. It’s getting late though—get some sleep, okay? I’ve got to get back in there. Love you!”

He blew me a kiss and ended the call.

I sat there, staring at the screen, unsure whether to feel reassured or suspicious. Gavin had always been an amazing husband. He was attractive, thoughtful, charming. When we first met, he hadn’t had a penny to his name.

He came from a modest background, raised in the city with a chronically ill younger sister. But out of all the men chasing after me, I chose him—because of his looks.

After college, I put up my parents’ house as collateral so we could start a supply business together. He handled sourcing; I handled clients—working so hard I nearly gave myself stomach ulcers. But in the end, we made it. The business took off.

When I got pregnant, I stepped back and let him take over the company so I could focus on raising our daughter and managing the household.

Macy had just turned four. We lived a comfortable, enviable life. People always said we were the perfect family. Gavin had always felt guilty we never had a wedding, so he went out of his way to spoil me, to make me feel loved.

How could a man like that cheat?

I bit my lip and smiled bitterly. Maybe I’d just watched one too many TV dramas. Still... that figure in the livestream stuck in my mind.

It was just for a second, but the gray windbreaker—wasn’t it the one I’d ironed for him before he left?

That thought nagged at me all night.

The next morning, Gavin came home early, arms full of sweets and snacks for Macy. He hugged us tightly, acting like the perfect, loving husband and father.

Feeling warm inside, I rushed into the kitchen to cook his favorite dishes as a welcome-home treat.

When we sat down to eat, Gavin glanced at me and said casually, “Smells like grease in here. Why don’t you take a shower?”

I sniffed the air and grinned. “That’s the smell of love, baby. You don’t like the scent of home-cooked food?”

He laughed and reached over to ruffle my hair. Then he gently popped a bite of food into my mouth, and gave Macy a piece too. “Alright, my girls. Let’s eat!”

After dinner, I got Macy ready for bed and then hopped in the shower myself. When I came back out, I leaned into Gavin, teasing, “Do I still smell like grease?”

He smiled and pinched my waist playfully. “God, I missed you.”

Before I could say another word, he pulled me onto the bed. He was more passionate than usual, as though he’d been starved for days.

Afterward, I lay there, breathless, watching his tall frame disappear into the bathroom.

I was about to clean up when his phone buzzed on the nightstand. A WhatsApp notification lit up the screen.

I glanced at it—and froze.

Chapter 2
I was just about to pick up his phone to see who the message was from when Gavin rushed back into the room and grabbed it before I could touch it. He glanced at the screen for a split second, then looked up at me.

“It’s Lily,” he said casually.

I narrowed my eyes. “What’s the matter? You worried I’ll find something?”

That uneasy feeling I had earlier returned full force. Something was off, and I could feel it in my bones.

The message had only four words: "Did she find out?"

That was all it took.

The words made my stomach turn. Whoever sent it clearly didn’t want me to know something—and Gavin was involved. My eyes locked on his face, searching for signs of guilt, of lies. And suddenly, everything in me screamed that something wasn’t right.

But Gavin just laughed it off and tossed the phone back onto the nightstand. Then he pulled me into his arms, kissing me softly.

“You’re overthinking it,” he murmured. “It’s not about you. Lily’s been using me as an excuse to pull one over on Mom again. She’s trying to get money out of her.”

Lily—Lilia Rhodes—was Gavin’s little sister. She had been frail and spoiled her whole life. The kind of girl who acted like a trust fund princess, even though they didn’t have that kind of money.

She was in her twenties now but still acted like a teenager. No job, no school—she just traveled, shopped, and partied like life was one long vacation.

“You’re helping her scam your own mother for money?” I snapped. “Where exactly do you think your mom’s money comes from?”

Gavin just grinned and scooped me up in his arms. His lips brushed against my ear as he carried me toward the bathroom. “Yeah, yeah, it’s all your money. That’s what happens when I marry a smart, successful woman like you.”

I couldn’t help but smile.

No matter what, I’d always been generous with his family. I believed in keeping peace, in being kind—because I knew harmony at home brought success in life. I treated them like my own, hoping they’d do the same.

The second round of intimacy in the shower washed away my doubts for the moment. Wrapped in Gavin’s arms afterward, I felt warm, comforted—even happy.

Later that night, I brought up something that had been weighing on me for a while: buying a new home in a good school district.

We’d been living in this tiny 500-square-foot apartment since we got married. I never minded the space, but now that Macy was about to start school, I couldn’t let her grow up with limited opportunities just because of our zip code.

We had been saving for years, but Gavin always said there was no rush. He wanted to wait for the perfect location in the city’s booming real estate market—so we wouldn’t have to move again and again.

But this time, he didn’t argue.

He kissed my forehead and whispered, “Alright, I’ll start looking. I’ll find a few places for you to check out, and you can choose what you like.”

His gentle tone reassured me. I fell asleep with a smile, dreaming of a beautiful, spacious new home where Macy could grow up safe and happy.

The next morning, after dropping Macy off at preschool, I got a call from my best friend, Elena. She wanted to meet for coffee at our usual spot.

Of course, I said yes.

Elena and I were like sisters. We could talk about anything. But it was rare for her to call me out of the blue—she was a busy woman, after all, working as a talent manager at a media company.

When I arrived at our favorite little dessert café, I spotted her in our corner booth, typing away on her laptop. The morning sunlight hit her just right, making her look even more striking.

She waved as I walked over, and I slid into the seat across from her, teasing, “Wow, you're actually free today? What’s the occasion?”

Elena rolled her eyes. “Am I not allowed to be concerned about my best friend?”

I laughed and took a sip of the coffee she ordered for me. “Sure you are. But you’re always the one who’s busy, while I’m the one with all the free time.”

“Pfft, you should be ashamed of that,” she said playfully, then added, “All I see these days is Gavin spoiling you. But hey, don’t say I didn’t warn you—don’t get too comfortable. That’s how people end up blind to what’s really going on.”

Her words hit a nerve.

I blinked, then looked at her more seriously. “What do you mean by that? You’re not just joking, are you?”

She glanced away, eyes flicking down to her laptop screen. “Relax. I’m just messing with you.”

But I wasn’t convinced. Something was off.

After a pause, she looked at me again and said, “I saw Gavin the day before yesterday.”

My heart skipped a beat. “Two days ago? Where?”

She raised an eyebrow. “What’s with that look?”

“Where did you see him?” I pressed, my voice sharper now.

Just then, her phone started ringing. She checked the screen and motioned for me to be quiet before answering. She spoke a few quick sentences, then her face changed.

“What? I’m on my way!”

She snapped her laptop shut and stuffed it into her bag. “I have to run. We’ll talk later, okay?”

“Wait, Elena—what were you—” I tried to stop her, but she was already out the door.

She said she saw Gavin two days ago.

But two days ago, Gavin was supposed to be out of town. In Darsen.

So where exactly did she see him?

Was she in Darsen too? Or was he... never there to begin with?

I slumped back in my seat, heart thudding painfully in my chest. Something was wrong. I could feel it in my gut.

That TikTok livestream kept replaying in my mind. I hadn’t gotten a good look, but... was it really him?

Was Gavin lying to me?

Was he cheating?

Chapter 3
I sat alone in the café, my thoughts spinning. Even with the warm sunlight streaming through the window, I couldn’t stop shivering. My mind kept circling the same question—what if Gavin was cheating? What would that mean for Macy?

I was so distracted the whole day that I completely forgot to pick Macy up from preschool. Luckily, Gavin came home early. When he realized I'd forgotten, he didn’t scold me. Instead, he gently reassured me before heading out to get her.

As soon as he left, I forced myself to get up and start dinner. But before Gavin and Macy returned, Lilia showed up unannounced. She had a spare key and treated our home like it was her own.

I didn’t like it, but Gavin always let her do whatever she wanted. When she saw me in the kitchen, she dropped her purse and walked over, leaning against the doorway.

“Why are you cooking? Where’s my brother?” she asked.

I was rinsing vegetables and replied without looking up. “He went to pick up Macy.”

“It’s this late and he’s only going now?” she said, her voice tinged with judgment. Lilia always acted spoiled and entitled, like she ran the place.

Her attitude toward me—her sister-in-law—was unpredictable. But I’d gotten used to it over the years. She was Gavin’s sister, after all. Marrying him meant accepting the good and the bad.

“Do we have any squid? I’m craving calamari,” she asked like it was her own kitchen.

I nodded toward the fridge. “Check in there. Gavin probably picked some up.”

Just then, Macy’s sweet voice echoed from the entryway. “Mommy, I’m home! Why didn’t you come get me today?” She ran over and looked up at me, her head tilted.

I felt a pang of guilt, but I smiled and pinched her nose with my damp fingers. “I got caught up with something. I promise I won’t forget you again, baby.”

Gavin stepped in behind her, carrying her tiny backpack. He smiled at the scene, then took off his coat and headed into the kitchen. Wrapping his arms around me from behind, he gently took off my apron and slipped it on himself.

“I’ve got this, honey. Go hang out with Macy,” he said softly.

Lilia, still standing nearby, rolled her eyes and said sarcastically, “Wow, my brother’s such a great husband. I need to find someone like him!”

“Get out of the kitchen and stop making a mess,” Gavin said, frowning. “Just wait for dinner to be ready.”

“I don’t want to. I’m helping!” she said in a sing-song voice, then pushed her way into the kitchen. “I want to see what it’s like to be a supportive wife!”

I sighed. She was unbelievable. How could she dream of marrying someone like her brother when she spent her days freeloading and doing nothing meaningful? Any guy who ended up with her would be cursed.

I was already on edge, and her presence only made it worse. She was a grown woman who constantly clung to Gavin like a child. I knew she was just buttering him up to ask for money again.

The Rhodes family had struggled for years. Gavin’s parents bounced between odd jobs, and Lilia was often sick, needing constant care. Life had been rough.

But things changed once my company started taking off. Gavin and I ended up supporting most of his family—including Lilia.

She acted like we owed her, constantly asking for money without any shame. She was like a leech, and yet she strutted around like she had nothing to worry about. I honestly didn’t know what to say anymore.

I took Macy’s hand and left the kitchen. Out of sight, out of mind. Just as we reached the hallway, my phone started ringing. When I checked, it was Elena.

I hurried to the bedroom to take the call and immediately started venting. “Seriously? You left me hanging earlier!”

“Work emergency,” she said tiredly. “I just finished dealing with it. That’s why I’m calling now. Why are you acting like I’ve got all the time in the world like you do?”

I hesitated for a second, then finally asked what had been bothering me all day. “Hey, the other day, you said you saw Gavin… Where was he? What time was it?”

There was a pause before she answered, calm and casual. “Honestly, I don’t remember exactly. I just saw him from my car while I was driving. It was a quick glimpse.”

“Oh.” Her vague answer left me uneasy. My heart sank, and I realized my palms were cold and clammy. I let out a dry laugh, wondering why I even wanted to find proof of Gavin cheating.

The truth was, he meant everything to me. The thought of losing him terrified me.

“You’re so obsessed with your husband, you know that?” Elena said. “You light up every time I mention his name. Can’t you start putting yourself first for once? Macy’s in school now—why not do something for yourself?”

“Don’t tell me you plan to live the rest of your life as Gavin’s shadow. You’re turning into a shell of a person. It’s like the world outside doesn’t exist to you anymore,” she continued.

I offered a weak smile and sighed. “Gavin said—”

“There it is again! ‘Gavin said this, Gavin said that.’” Elena snapped. “See what I mean? Your whole world revolves around him. If he told you to jump off a cliff, would you? If he tried to sell you, would you help him close the deal and count the money?”

“Ugh, you’re such a downer! Gavin would never do that!” I shot back.

“Yeah, maybe he wouldn’t. But I would!” she laughed bitterly. “Look, the truth hurts, but you’ve gotta have some self-worth. Being a housewife isn’t the problem—it’s when your whole identity disappears into it. That’s not love. That’s blind devotion.

“Love means he actually cares about you, sees you. How do you expect to keep his attention when all you do is stay home and take care of chores? Let me ask you something: besides being a mom and a wife, do you even know who you are anymore?”

She kept talking, and I didn’t even have the energy to argue back.

She caught onto my silence and softened her tone.

“Mira, I just want to see you shine again,” she said gently. “You used to be so confident, so full of life. You were always the top of the class—my superstar! It just breaks my heart to see you wasting away at home like this, stuck in this routine.”

“Okay, that’s enough,” I said, half-laughing. “You’re giving me a pep talk after slapping me in the face. Seriously, who pissed you off today that you had to take it out on me?”

We both laughed at that.

Even so, I knew Elena always spoke her mind. She’d said similar things before, but for some reason, this time it hit different. Her words left me uneasy, and I couldn’t shake the feeling that she was hinting at something more.

Just then, there was a soft knock at the door. Gavin walked in with a warm smile.

“Babe, dinner’s ready.”

Elena heard his voice through the phone and said, “Alright, go eat. But think about what I said, okay? Don’t get blinded by the shiny things right in front of you. Sometimes the truth hides in the shadows.”

And with that, she hung up.

Gavin pulled me into his arms and kissed me lightly. “Who was that?”

“Elena.”

“What’d she say this time? Still preaching?” he teased with a soft smile. He knew how close the three of us were—we’d all gone to school together. “I haven’t seen her in forever.”

His words made my thoughts swirl again. He said he hadn’t seen her in a long time… So if Elena had spotted him, it must’ve been from far away. Maybe it really was just a coincidence. I felt a wave of relief wash over me, realizing I might’ve been overthinking everything.

But Gavin noticed my distraction. He tilted his head and looked at me closely, then gently pinched both my cheeks and leaned in for another kiss. His touch was tender, full of concern.

“What’s going on in that head of yours?” he asked. “What’s got you so distracted?”

His eyes searched mine, but I quickly pulled myself together and smiled. “Nothing. Let’s go eat.”

He wrapped his arm around me and kissed me again before we walked out of the room together.

Still, deep down, the doubt in my heart only grew heavier.

Chapter 4
Lilia didn’t stick around long after dinner. She pouted at Gavin and said, “Gav, can you give me a ride?”

I rolled my eyes and glanced her way, but she played dumb, clinging to Gavin’s arm like a spoiled little princess.

Gavin looked at me with a sheepish smile, clearly caught in the middle. When I didn’t say anything, he awkwardly offered, “Just hang on a bit. I’ll help Mira with the dishes first, then I’ll take you.”

Honestly, I’d had enough of Lilia’s antics and didn’t want to deal with her a second longer. I waved Gavin off. “Go ahead. Take her wherever she wants to go. I’ve got the dishes.”

“Daddy, where are you going? I wanna come too!” Macy called out, standing up from her chair and stretching out her tiny arms for Gavin to lift her.

He picked her up and kissed her cheek. “Daddy will be back soon! Be a good girl and stay with Mommy, okay?”

“What’s the point of bringing the kid?” Lilia muttered, clearly annoyed.

I took Macy into my arms and said gently, “Sweetie, Daddy’s just giving your aunt a ride. He’ll be back soon. Can you stay with Mommy till then?”

Macy looked up at me with her big, tear-brimmed eyes, then nodded and hugged my neck tight before turning to Gavin. “Okay! Come home soon, Daddy!”

Gavin kissed her again and nodded. “I will.”

He grabbed the car keys and left with Lilia hanging onto his arm. She threw me a smug, knowing smile over her shoulder, but I couldn’t bring myself to care.

Gavin didn’t get home until late that night, but I didn’t press him. He was always a dutiful son, and I figured he probably spent time chatting with his parents before heading back.

The next morning, he got up early, saying he had an important meeting at nine. He even took Macy with him and dropped her off at preschool to save me the hassle.

Gavin always paid attention to the little things. He left me no room to complain. Just like Elena once said—he pampered me so much, I got used to it. To everyone around us, he was the perfect husband.

I noticed the clothes he’d changed out of and decided to tidy up a bit since laundry had been piling up. Before taking them to the dry cleaners, I checked the pockets—and that’s when I found it.

A condom. Still in its wrapper.

My heart dropped.

It was solid proof. There was no reason for him to have that. I had an IUD since giving birth to Macy. We didn’t use protection anymore. My stomach turned. I tossed the damn thing in the trash, but the damage was done. My world cracked open.

He was cheating on me.

After everything we’d been through, after all the sacrifices, he betrayed me.

Just when life was finally looking up, he dared to lie to me like this. I collapsed to the floor, clutching my head. My mind was flooded with cruel images of him with another woman.

I’d given him everything—my youth, my love, my loyalty. I gave everything I had to him and this family. And this is how he repaid me?

I whispered to myself, over and over again, “Mira, pull it together. You can’t lose everything now.”

I needed the truth. A definitive answer.

Once I calmed down, I clenched my fists and forced myself not to fall apart. After a long, steady breath, I freshened up, called a cab, and headed to the company.

I’d only been to Bright Corporation once, back when they first moved into the new building in Solara Heights. Gavin took me there and proudly showed me the entire floor we were renting. It was a big moment for both of us.

That day, he held me by the floor-to-ceiling windows and said, “Thank you for helping me, Mira. You changed my life. I swear, babe, one day that whole building’s gonna be yours.”

I’d laughed then. And now, standing outside, all I could think was—he was about to destroy everything we built.

When I walked into the lobby, the young, pretty receptionist smiled and asked where I was headed and who I needed to see. I told her I was looking for Gavin.

She gave me a once-over and smiled politely. “I’m sorry, ma’am. Mr. Rhodes isn’t in. He left earlier with his wife.”

Her words hit me like a slap in the face. I’d tried to prepare myself, but hearing it out loud still sent a jolt through me. I gripped my purse tighter and asked, a little too sharply, “What did you say? Are you sure?”

She looked confused. “Yes, ma’am. You said Mr. Gavin Rhodes from the 10th floor, right? He left this morning—with his wife.”

The way she said it, so sure of herself, made my blood run cold.

I wanted to scream—If she’s his wife, then who the hell am I?

But I bit my tongue, clenched my jaw, and walked out of Solara Heights with whatever dignity I had left. Maybe the receptionist made a mistake. Maybe there was still a chance to protect Gavin’s reputation. Maybe...

Still, I needed confirmation.

I called Samuel Ortiz, one of the senior guys in marketing—someone who would know Gavin’s schedule. My hands were trembling as I dialed, but I steadied my voice.

“Hey, Sam. Has Gavin finished his meeting? I’ve been trying to reach him, but he’s not answering. Getting a little worried.”

He sounded puzzled. “Meeting? There’s no meeting today, Mrs. Rhodes. Mr. Rhodes went out.”

That’s all I needed to hear. “Oh,” I said quietly and hung up.

I felt like the ground disappeared beneath me. My knees gave out, my body went numb, and my hand shook violently.

I couldn’t even bring myself to call Gavin. What was the point? Even if I asked, he’d just lie again. I didn’t believe a word he said anymore.

He was strutting around Solara Heights with another woman on his arm, letting everyone believe she was his wife. She had the nerve to walk into the company I helped build, enjoy the perks I earned, act like she belonged.

I stood there in the middle of the crowd, completely lost. He was slipping through my fingers like sand. The tighter I held, the faster he escaped.

But then, things started to click. I figured out who this so-called “Mrs. Rhodes” was.

And with that realization, I pushed through the numbness, flagged down a cab, and headed home. I stopped by the market and picked up ingredients for all of Gavin’s favorite dishes. I even bought some fresh pineapple for Macy.

I was going to wait for him.

As I moved around the kitchen, prepping everything, my mind raced with what to do next.

I’d always thought time flew too fast. But that day, it dragged like never before.

When night fell, I finally picked up the phone, called Gavin calmly, and asked where he was. Then I told him to pick Macy up.

He agreed without hesitation.

Chapter 5
I was just about done prepping dinner when Gavin came back with our daughter. Macy burst through the door, her sweet little voice bubbling with joy. “Mommy, I’m home! Daddy picked me up!”

Her innocent excitement tugged at my heartstrings, and I had to fight back the tears. “I got you some pineapple—your favorite, right?”

“Oh! Mommy, you’re the best! I can’t wait to eat it!” She dashed off toward Gavin, shouting, “Daddy, I want some pineapple!”

“You can have a small piece now. The rest after dinner, okay?” Gavin replied, rinsing his hands before handing her a little slice.

Then he squeezed into the tiny kitchen behind me and wrapped his arms around my waist. “Why’d you make so much food?”

His touch made my stomach turn. This used to be a happy home, the three of us. Now it felt like everything was falling apart.

“You just got back from your business trip. You must be exhausted,” I said, forcing a smile. “Busy day?”

He answered with a nonchalant hum, and my heart sank. I nudged him with my elbow, trying to keep things light. “Go set the table. Dinner’s almost ready.”

His affection felt fake—rehearsed. I couldn’t help but wonder if he was thinking about her when he touched me. Once I finished cooking, I turned to him with a smile and asked, “Want a drink? It’s been a while—I could use a glass of wine.”

He looked at me, a little surprised. “What’s the occasion? Why the sudden urge to drink?”

“No real reason. Just wondering if you’re heading out again later,” I said as I grabbed the wine. “I made all this food… feels like we should celebrate.”

The words felt like glass in my throat. I knew Gavin couldn’t hold his liquor well, so I only poured him a small amount to avoid raising suspicion. I gave myself half a glass and held it up for a toast.

As we drank, the atmosphere shifted. We got chatty, almost giddy. I pretended to be in a good mood, laughing as I reminisced about college, the early days of building our business, and the life we’d created since. I looked like the picture of happiness.

Gavin noticed my good mood and poured himself another glass, cautioning me not to overdo it. But in the end, he drank more than he should have. By the time I helped him into bed, he was already drunk.

After cleaning up and tucking Macy in for the night, I started what I had planned all along. My heart pounded—it had been years since I’d snooped through his things. I finally realized how naive I’d been to trust him so blindly.

I rifled through his pockets and his bag, but there was nothing useful.

Then I spotted his phone—but it was locked with a fingerprint. I crept over to the bed and gently grabbed his hand, holding my breath. As I tried to unlock it, he suddenly stirred and turned toward me, his eyes glassy and unfocused. My heart nearly stopped.

“I need water,” he mumbled.

I raced out to get him a glass, brought it back, and helped him drink. Seconds later, he collapsed onto the bed, fully out.

I pressed his finger to the sensor and unlocked the phone. I started scrolling through his call history—nothing suspicious. Most of the names were familiar, and hardly any were women.

Next, I opened WhatsApp. He hadn’t been chatting much. I clicked on the first contact and saw a single message from the day he came home.

“Did she find out?”

Just those four words. Nothing else. It didn’t look like he’d deleted anything either. I tapped on the woman’s profile photo, hoping to find something—anything—but there were no posts, no updates. Nothing.

There were no clues to who she was. Whoever she was, she clearly knew how to cover her tracks. Gavin had told me it was Lilia. But I couldn’t just take his word for it—I needed proof.

Gavin’s phone gallery had photos of Macy and me—and just two of Lilia. Aside from that, everything looked clean. I even ran a scan using a security app, but nothing suspicious came up. That night, I tossed and turned, unable to understand how there were no traces of anything.

I started thinking—whoever that woman was, she clearly wasn’t someone from Gavin’s office or our apartment building. If she had been, the receptionist wouldn’t have called her Mrs. Rhodes.

Who was she? Had I met her before without realizing it?

The next morning, I dragged myself out of bed, dark circles haunting my reflection in the mirror.

Gavin noticed my worn-out face right away. “Mimi, are you feeling okay? You look really pale.”

“You kept me up all night,” I snapped, not in the mood to pretend everything was fine.

He blinked, clearly caught off guard, then gave me a sheepish smile and hugged me. “No more wine for you. You should try working out instead—it helps with sleep.”

For some reason, his words made my stomach turn. I ran to the bathroom, barely making it in time before I started vomiting. Tears streamed down my face.

Gavin followed me in and knelt beside me, gently patting my back. “Babe, what’s wrong? Maybe we should go to the hospital.”

I pushed his hand away and lied through my teeth. “I’m fine. Just didn’t sleep well. You should take Macy to school—I just need to rest a little more.”

He helped me back to bed and tucked me in like everything was normal. “Alright, get some sleep. I’ll drop Macy off. If you start feeling worse, call me right away, okay?”

I nodded.

I lay there listening to their voices fade as they left. When I heard the front door close, I jumped out of bed and ran to the window. I watched as Gavin walked Macy to the car, her tiny hand swinging in his. She looked so happy.

I didn’t take my eyes off them until the car rolled out of the gated community. Then the tears came. I couldn’t help but wonder: what if things could just go back to the way they used to be?

I pulled myself together, throwing on jeans, a t-shirt, and tied my hair into a ponytail. A baseball cap topped it off. Then I headed out.

I found a seat at the café across from Solara Heights—a spot with the perfect view of the entrance. I knew it was a long shot, but it felt like my best option.

Three days passed. I sat there every morning, sipping coffee, waiting. But I never saw Gavin—not even once. That’s when I realized the flaw in my plan: Gavin usually parked in the underground garage, which had a private passage straight into the building. I’d completely overlooked that.

It finally clicked on the fourth day.

Just when I was about to give up, I saw Gavin coming out of the building, phone in hand, walking briskly. He was talking to someone and heading in the direction of St. Lewis Square.

My heart started racing. He wasn’t in his car, and it wasn’t lunchtime, so he must not be going far. I followed from a distance as he crossed the street and entered a stylish café—chic, upscale, the kind of place frequented by professionals discussing deals or catching up with clients.

I figured he was meeting someone. I shifted closer to the floor-to-ceiling windows, debating whether I should follow him in.

That’s when I spotted her—sitting upstairs by the window in a rose-pink pantsuit that looked bold and elegant. It was Elena.

She was stunning, more put together than usual. I actually laughed to myself, thinking what a funny coincidence it was that she happened to be there. It meant I didn’t have to sneak around—Elena could see who Gavin was meeting.

Relaxed by the thought, I picked up my phone and called her.

I watched as Elena looked at the screen and answered. But then something strange happened—Gavin appeared behind her, right at the window.

She turned slightly and subtly held a finger to her lips, signaling Gavin to stay quiet. Then her voice came through the phone.

“Are you just bored or something?” she said playfully.

Her words hit me like a slap. If this had been before, I might’ve laughed it off as friendly banter. But now, it felt like mockery. Like she was playing a role in some cruel inside joke.

That hurt more than seeing her with Gavin.

I asked quietly, “Where are you?”

“I’m in a meeting at the office. I’ll call you back later,” she said, still looking directly at Gavin as she spoke.

I was speechless.

I never thought my best friend would lie to me. I never imagined she could betray me like this.

Chapter 6
I let out a bitter smile and said, “Alright,” before ending the call. Elena had become manipulative in my eyes. She acted like she genuinely cared, advising me to reflect on myself, but then she turned around and mocked me right in front of my husband.

It finally hit me how unpredictable people could be. No wonder she had tried to fish for information earlier by claiming she saw Gavin—it was all because of her guilt.

Gavin had told me he hadn’t seen Elena in a long time. My heart sank at the realization that he had lied to me. I had invested so much trust in both of them after coming to this unfamiliar city, and now I felt utterly betrayed. I didn’t know who I could trust anymore.

I stared out the window for a long while before finally calling Gavin. Just as I suspected, his answer matched Elena’s word for word.

Anger surged through me, and I stormed out toward the café. But just as I walked in, my phone rang. It was Macy’s preschool teacher—she told me Macy had fallen off the slide and had been taken to the hospital. My heart stopped. I immediately flagged down a cab and rushed over.

On the way, I called Gavin to let him know what had happened.

We both arrived at Beacon Hope Hospital at nearly the same time. There was Macy in the emergency room, crying with a scrape on her forehead. The doctor explained she had a mild concussion—she had vomited after the fall and needed to be monitored overnight for safety.

The teacher in charge of Macy looked pale and tearful, her eyes filled with guilt as she looked at Gavin. The school’s director was there too, apologizing over and over.

Gavin, although clearly upset, stayed calm and asked the director about the accident. She said another child had pushed Macy off the slide’s platform.

That made my blood run cold—the slide was at least five feet high.

“Do you people even care about the kids at your school?! We trust you to watch over our children, and this is what happens?!” I shouted, unable to hold back my fury.

Gavin looked at me, stunned. He’d never seen me this emotional before. Even Macy was frightened, trembling as she continued to cry.

Gavin tried to calm me while the director handled the hospital paperwork and arranged a room for Macy. Once everything was settled, Elena called me, asking where I was.

I figured she already knew. Still, I told her Macy had been hurt and was in the hospital. A short while later, Elena showed up, acting all concerned as she asked about Macy’s condition.

Gavin was still in the room when she arrived. They both looked composed, though I caught a subtle look pass between them. Gavin even looked a little uneasy.

I kept my cool and pretended not to notice. Then I asked Elena, “Done with your meeting already?”

“Yeah. It wasn’t anything major,” she answered casually, then added, “Did you need something?”

“Not really. I was just bored. Gavin mentioned he hadn’t seen you in a while, so I thought maybe we could grab lunch sometime,” I said, watching her closely.

She gave me a quick glance and responded, “Oh, come on. Let’s wait until Macy’s feeling better. I’ll take your whole family out for a nice meal.”

She reached out to gently stroke Macy’s head. “Sound good, Macy? I’ll buy you whatever you want when you’re all better.”

Macy gave a small nod, pouting. Her forehead was swollen from the fall, and it broke my heart.

Without thinking, I brushed Elena’s hand away. The sight of her trying to play the caring "stepmom" infuriated me. Was she already planning on replacing me? I wasn’t about to let that happen.

Elena noticed my cold reaction and looked confused. “Is something wrong?” she asked softly.

Before I could say anything, Gavin jumped in. “She’s just not feeling well.”

He gently placed a hand on my shoulder. “Don’t worry, sweetheart. The doctor said Macy’s going to be fine. We can go home once they finish observing her.”

“Home?” That word hit me like a punch. I suddenly stood up, shoved Gavin’s hand away, and ran out of the room, sobbing. This family was already falling apart, and now the woman who might become my daughter’s stepmother was standing right there, acting like she belonged.

Elena chased after me, and Macy started crying again.

“Mira, what’s wrong with you? Don’t scare Macy like that,” Elena said, grabbing my arm. “You need to pull it together—for the kid’s sake.”

“Pull it together? Really?!” I snapped, glaring at her.

I realized I was spiraling and tried to calm myself, but I couldn’t stop shaking. My lips trembled as I said, “Just go. We’re fine. You don’t have to pause your busy life for us!”

Then I brushed past her and walked back into the room, wiping my tears. Inside, Gavin was comforting Macy. I went straight to him and pulled him away, tears pouring down my face.

Gavin looked at me, stunned. “It’s okay… Don’t stress yourself too much. You’re scaring Macy.”

Elena walked in awkwardly, clearly unsure what to do. She smacked her lips a few times, and the air turned heavy.

“Mira, I’ll head out. No need to get too worked up. Just call me if you need anything,” she said, trying to keep her tone light before turning to Macy. “Sweetie, I’m leaving, alright? Get better soon, and I’ll bring you something yummy!”

I turned to Gavin, wiping away my tears. “Didn’t you say you hadn’t seen Elena in a long time? Then go ahead—walk her out.”

Gavin’s expression shifted briefly, but then he smiled. “Alright. Just… don’t cry anymore, okay?”

He walked Elena out of the room. As they stepped into the hallway, I heard Elena say, “No need to walk me out. Stay with Macy. I’ll drop by again if I can.”

Her footsteps faded as Gavin returned to the room.

“Honey, what’s wrong?” he asked.

“You really don’t know?” I said, eyes red and puffy. Macy started crying again, so I leaned down and kissed her cheek.

“It’s okay, baby. Mommy’s here,” I whispered.

And then I started crying again too. Mommy would always be here—forever. But what about Daddy? If we got divorced… what would happen to you, Macy?

I was shaken that the thought even crossed my mind.

The afternoon dragged on. People from the preschool came by to check on things. Even the boy’s parents showed up. It was a constant stream of visitors until late in the evening, and I felt drained.

Macy finally drifted off to sleep, and I stayed right by her side. The doctor had warned us to keep her still—no sudden movements allowed.

Gavin was out in the hallway, making phone calls, while I sat quietly by Macy’s bedside, watching her sleep. My heart was in a storm of emotions. Gavin could tell something was off, so he stayed close, just in case. He didn’t leave the hospital that night—and honestly, I wasn’t going to let him.

As I watched him lying on the edge of the hospital bed, a wave of conflicting feelings washed over me. If I hadn’t found out he was cheating, I probably would’ve told him to go home and rest. He still had work to do, after all.

But everything had changed now. Gavin was Macy’s father—he had a responsibility to be here. Even if he didn’t love me anymore, he damn well better love his daughter.

After three days in the hospital, the doctor finally gave us the green light to take Macy home. Gavin suggested she should rest a few more days before going back to school. Since he had already taken some time off, he had to head straight back to work.

I watched him walk out the door, and all I could think was how eager he probably was to run back to his mistress. He'd been stuck with me for days and now had his freedom again. That sly fox—he played the part of a caring father and husband so well. What else was he doing behind my back if he could look me in the eyes and lie without flinching?

A few days later, Elena called to check in on Macy. I kept my answers short and cold. Just hearing her voice made me tense up. I couldn’t stop thinking about how she had lied to my face while sneaking around with Gavin. The betrayal cut deep—not just from him, but from her too.

I couldn’t shake the thought—what if she was the “Mrs. Rhodes” the receptionist had mentioned? What if it really was her?

And if it was… what then?

That was the first time the thought of divorce seriously crossed my mind. Maybe I didn’t have to beg, cry, or fight.

Maybe I could make Gavin pay.

Maybe I could take everything from him… and leave him with nothing.

title: This Changes Everything
body:
I found a lump on my granddaughter's neck, and it led me to discover what's really crawling on your family's produce.
 
The produce industry doesn't want you to know this.
 
And the companies selling you vinegar washes and twelve-dollar produce sprays are praying you never find out.
 
Hi, my name is Dakota, I'm a fifty-eight-year-old grandmother, and I've always prided myself on keeping a clean, welcoming kitchen.
 
The kind of home where my granddaughter Lily begged to stay for dinner and my husband Tom swore my cooking was the best in the county.
 
I bought fresh fruits and vegetables every week.
 
Rinsed everything under the tap before serving it.
 
I even kept a colander by the sink so I could rinse berries the second I got home from the store, just like my mother taught me.
 
But a few months ago, everything changed.
 
It started on a Saturday.
 
Lily had spent the afternoon at our house.
 
I made her favorite salad with spinach and strawberries and she snacked on grapes all afternoon.
 
She was fine.
 
Happy.
 
Normal.
 
Three days later, my daughter called.
 
Mom, Lily has a lump on her neck.
 
The doctor said it's a swollen lymph node.
 
My heart stopped.
 
He asked what she ate recently, my daughter continued.
 
I told him about the strawberries and grapes at your house.
 
There was a pause.
 
Then she said the words that kept me awake for three nights straight.
 
I'm not blaming you Mom, but the doctor said parasites and bacteria on produce can cause this in children.
 
My face went hot.
 
My hands were shaking.
 
I looked across the kitchen at the fruit bowl on the counter.
 
The same strawberries I had rinsed under the tap that morning.
 
The same grapes I thought were clean because I'd run water over them.
 
The same produce I thought was the healthiest thing I could feed my granddaughter.
 
Tom tried to calm me down.
 
Kids get swollen lymph nodes all the time, he said.
 
It could be anything.
 
But I couldn't let it go.
 
That night, after Tom went to bed, I started researching.
 
What I found kept me up until two in the morning.
 
And it wasn't just pesticides.
 
It was parasites.
 
Microscopic parasite eggs and larvae live on the surface of produce.
 
They come from contaminated soil. From irrigation water that contains animal waste. From workers handling food in fields with no sanitation. From shipping containers and conveyor belts that haven't been cleaned in months.
 
Roundworm. Hookworm. Tapeworm larvae. Toxoplasma. Cryptosporidium.
 
These aren't rare tropical diseases.
 
They are on grocery store produce in America right now.
 
The CDC estimates that more than sixty million Americans are carrying parasitic infections and most of them have no idea.
 
Because the symptoms don't look like parasites.
 
They look like bloating.
 
Stomach cramps.
 
Fatigue.
 
Swollen lymph nodes.
 
Unexplained weight changes.
 
Skin issues.
 
Brain fog.
 
Symptoms that doctors attribute to stress, diet, IBS, or age.
 
And the whole time, the actual cause is living in your gut, feeding off what you eat, because it hitched a ride on a strawberry you rinsed under the tap for three seconds.
 
A quick rinse under the tap removes maybe twenty to thirty percent of what's on your produce.
 
That's it.
 
Parasite eggs are microscopic.
 
They cling to the waxy surface of your produce.
 
They survive cold water.
 
They survive refrigeration.
 
Some of them survive stomach acid.
 
Running water over a strawberry was never going to wash off something designed by evolution to survive inside a human body.
 
And children are more vulnerable than adults.
 
Their immune systems are still developing.
 
Their smaller bodies can't fight off parasitic infections the way an adult can.
 
What gives a grown adult mild bloating can give a five-year-old swollen lymph nodes and a fever.
 
That's when the real panic set in.
 
The next morning, I watched Lily's little brother reach for a grape from the fruit bowl and I grabbed his hand before he could put it in his mouth.
 
I stared at the grape.
 
At the fruit bowl.
 
At the bag of spinach in the fridge.
 
In that moment, three things hit me at once.
 
This wasn't about dirty produce.
 
This wasn't coming off with water.
 
And this wasn't something I could keep ignoring.
 
That evening, I tried everything I could find.
 
First, the vinegar soak.
 
I mixed a solution in a bowl and dropped the strawberries in.
 
Twenty minutes later, the berries tasted like vinegar.
 
The kids wouldn't touch them.
 
And when I looked it up, vinegar doesn't kill parasite eggs.
 
It can weaken some bacteria on the outer surface but parasite eggs have a protective shell that vinegar cannot penetrate.
 
Next, baking soda.
 
Scrubbing each piece of produce by hand in a baking soda paste.
 
It took over twenty minutes to get through a single bowl of fruit.
 
Messy, tedious, and according to the research, it does not destroy parasitic organisms.
 
Tom tried a commercial produce wash spray he grabbed from the grocery store.
 
Twelve dollars for a bottle of what was essentially just another chemical sitting on our food.
 
The reviews were brutal.
 
One person asked if her bottle had gone rancid or if they'd changed the formula.
 
It smelled horrible either way.
 
And nowhere on the label did it mention parasites.
 
I even looked into buying everything organic.
 
But organic doesn't mean parasite-free.
 
Organic produce grows in the same soil.
 
Gets irrigated with the same water.
 
Gets handled by the same hands.
 
Gets shipped on the same trucks.
 
Parasites don't care if your produce is organic.
 
Every path forward had a problem.
 
Every option was incomplete.
 
I've tried EVERYTHING, I told Tom one night.
 
Nothing actually works.
 
And Lily's doctor is asking about our food.
 
Then my neighbor Sarah changed everything.
 
Sarah is a mom of two who cares about food safety the way I now cared about it.
 
Over coffee one morning, I mentioned the lump on Lily's neck, the constant anxiety about produce, the guilt every time I handed the kids a piece of fruit.
 
I asked her, how do you handle the produce thing?
 
I've tried vinegar, baking soda, those sprays, literally everything.
 
Nothing shows me it's actually working.
 
Sarah's face went serious.
 
Wait here, she said.
 
I need to show you something.
 
She reached into her bag and pulled out a small, dark navy blue capsule-shaped device.
 
It fit in the palm of her hand.
 
Barely bigger than a salt shaker.
 
Trust me, she said.
 
I tried every single thing you've tried.
 
The vinegar soak that leaves an aftertaste.
 
The baking soda mess.
 
Those sprays that are just another chemical on your food.
 
None of it kills parasites.
 
Then I found this.
 
Drop it in a bowl of water with your produce.
 
Ten minutes later you'll see everything that was hiding on your clean fruits and vegetables.
 
Pesticides. Wax. Bacteria.
 
And sometimes things you really wish you hadn't seen.
 
I was skeptical.
 
After everything I'd tried, how could something this small actually work?
 
But that afternoon, I filled a bowl with water, dropped in the strawberries I had just bought, and placed the device in the bowl.
 
I set a timer for ten minutes and went to fold laundry.
 
When I came back, I literally gasped.
 
The water had turned cloudy brown.
 
There was an oily film floating on the surface.
 
I touched it.
 
It felt waxy.
 
And floating in the water, barely visible unless you looked closely, were tiny thread-like strands.
 
I fished one out with a fork.
 
It was a worm.
 
A tiny, translucent worm that had been on the strawberries I was about to give my grandchildren.
 
Strawberries I had already rinsed under the tap.
 
I stood there staring at that bowl for a long time.
 
Not because of the wax or the cloudy water.
 
Because of the worm.
 
Because of Lily.
 
Because of all the Saturdays I'd handed her strawberries thinking I was giving her something healthy.
 
Not knowing what was clinging to the surface.
 
Not knowing what she was swallowing with every bite.
 
The small device had a label that read PurePod.
 
I immediately looked it up.
 
Turns out, it uses something called Ion Purification Technology, a scientific breakthrough originally developed for commercial food safety and industrial produce decontamination.
 
Here's how it works.
 
The device generates powerful ions that break apart pesticide residues, wax coatings, bacteria, and parasitic organisms at the molecular level.
 
The ions destroy the protective shells around parasite eggs that water, vinegar, and baking soda cannot penetrate.
 
They disrupt the cellular structure of larvae and adult parasites on contact.
 
They force everything off the surface of your produce and into the water.
 
Unlike vinegar or baking soda that only clean the outer surface, Ion Purification Technology destroys organisms that have evolved to survive everything your kitchen can throw at them.
 
It reaches what hands, brushes, and soaks never could.
 
And because nothing is added, no soaps, no sprays, no chemicals, the only byproducts are water and oxygen.
 
No aftertaste.
 
No residue.
 
No mess.
 
This same technology is widely used in commercial food processing facilities for Michelin-star restaurants, where parasite-free, chemical-free produce decontamination at scale is a critical requirement.
 
No wonder the companies selling you twelve-dollar spray bottles that go rancid and the organic industry charging a thousand dollars a year extra don't want you to know about this.
 
It makes everything they sell completely unnecessary.
 
That's why PurePod isn't in stores.
 
You won't find it at any big retailer because it cuts into their profits on replacement sprays, washes, and the organic premium.
 
It's only available on the official website.
 
The results kept getting better.
 
Berries that used to get fuzzy by Wednesday started lasting the entire week.
 
The fruit actually tasted better too.
 
Sweeter, cleaner, the way fruit is supposed to taste when it's not coated in wax and contamination.
 
Tom's stomach issues cleared up within two weeks.
 
The bloating he'd had for months disappeared.
 
He stopped reaching for the antacids after every meal.
 
The random stomach complaints that had been running through our family for months just stopped.
 
And Lily?
 
Lily's lump went down within a week.
 
The doctor said her lymph nodes were back to normal.
 
My daughter started letting her eat at grandma's house again.
 
I didn't fully realize how contaminated our produce had been until everyone stopped getting sick and the fruit started lasting twice as long.
 
I ordered two more that same week.
 
One for my daughter's house so Lily would be protected wherever she ate, and one for my travel bag because PurePod is smaller than a soda can with a battery that lasts two hundred fifty minutes.
 
It works in any bowl, any sink, any hotel room.
 
Within a month, Tom was running the Sunday produce batch himself.
 
Three neighbors had already ordered their own after I sent the dirty water photo to the group chat.
 
I didn't send the worm photo.
 
Some things you don't want to see over breakfast.
 
Since then, I've told everyone I know.
 
My sister got one.
 
My book club friends got them.
 
Every single person who's tried it has had the same reaction.
 
They can't believe they've been feeding their families produce carrying parasites, pesticide residues, and bacteria when this existed the whole time.
 
One friend told me she was spending an extra hundred and twenty dollars a month buying organic for just the Dirty Dozen items.
 
She got a PurePod and started saving money.
 
Her produce is cleaner now than organic ever was, and she's saving over a thousand dollars a year.
 
Another friend, a single grandmother raising grandchildren on a fixed income, said she'd been throwing away half her berries by Wednesday every single week.
 
PurePod solved it.
 
Her food lasts dramatically longer now, and her grandkids are eating fresher, safer meals on the same budget.
 
Right now, the company behind PurePod is offering up to seventy percent off, but I don't know how long that's going to last.
 
Every time word spreads about this device, it sells out fast.
 
Last time they completely sold out their inventory within seventy-two hours.
 
That's why it's not in stores and you won't find it on Amazon.
 
It's only available on the official website and supplies are extremely limited.
 
If you're rinsing your produce under the tap and hoping for the best, if you've cycled through the vinegar and baking soda and sprays and none of it showed you proof, if you feel that knot in your stomach every time you hand your grandchild a piece of fruit, you need to see this.
 
One PurePod costs less than what most families spend on organic produce in a single week and it never needs replacing.
 
No filters.
 
No refills.
 
No subscriptions.
 
One purchase.
 
The company backs it with a ninety-day money-back guarantee.
 
If PurePod doesn't change how you feel about your family's produce, you get every penny back, no questions asked.
 
That's three full months to test it in your own kitchen with zero risk.
 
I spent months stressing over what was making my family sick.
